title.zh: 卷416 列傳二百三 程学启 何安泰 郑国魁 刘铭傳 张树珊弟：树屏 周盛波
title.en: Volume 416 Biographies 203: Cheng Xueqi, He Antai, Zheng Guokui, Liu Mingchuan, Zhang Shushan younger brother: Shu Ping, Zhou Shengbo
title.raw: 卷416 列傳二百三 程学启 何安泰 郑国魁 刘铭傳 张树珊弟：树屏 周盛波

sentences.zh: 程學啟，字方忠，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Cheng Xueqi, styled Fangzhong, was a man of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xueqi, whose courtesy name was Fangzhong, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 初陷賊中，陳玉成奇其勇，使佐葉芸來守安慶。

translations.literal: At first he fell among the rebels; Chen Yucheng regarded his bravery as extraordinary and had him assist Ye Yunlai in guarding Anqing.
translations.idiomatic: He had first been trapped in rebel territory, but Chen Yucheng took notice of his courage and assigned him to assist Ye Yunlai in the defense of Anqing.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，率三百人自拔來歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, he led three hundred men to break free and come over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Xianfeng reign (1861), he led three hundred men in breaking away from the rebels and defecting to the Qing side.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃使領一營，戰輒請先。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan had him command one battalion; in battle he always asked to go first.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan put him in command of a battalion, and in every engagement he volunteered to lead the assault.

sentences.zh: 安慶北門石壘三最堅，學啟力攻拔之，絕賊糧道。

translations.literal: The three stone forts at Anqing's north gate were the stoutest; Xueqi attacked with force and captured them, cutting off the rebels' grain route.
translations.idiomatic: The three stone redoubts at Anqing's north gate were the hardest to crack; Xueqi stormed and took them, severing the rebels' supply line.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂克安慶，學啟功最，擢游擊，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Before long Anqing was taken; Xueqi's merit was foremost, and he was promoted to acting major and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Anqing fell; Xueqi's contribution ranked first, and he was promoted to brevet major and awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 從國荃克無為、銅陵諸城，擢參將。

translations.literal: Following Guoquan he captured Wuwei, Tongling, and other cities, and was promoted to lieutenant colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Guoquan, he helped take Wuwei, Tongling, and other towns, and was raised to the rank of colonel.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率淮軍規江蘇，請於曾國籓，以學啟隸麾下。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Li Hongzhang led the Huai Army in a campaign against Jiangsu and requested of Zeng Guofan that Xueqi be placed under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862), Li Hongzhang led the Huai Army in operations to recover Jiangsu and asked Zeng Guofan to assign Xueqi to his staff.

sentences.zh: 瀕行，國籓勉之曰：「江南人譽張國樑不去口，汝好為之，亦一國樑也！」

translations.literal: On the eve of departure Guofan exhorted him, saying: "The people of Jiangnan speak of Zhang Guoliang without ceasing; do well, and you too may be a Guoliang!"
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, Guofan urged him: "In Jiangnan they never stop praising Zhang Guoliang—apply yourself, and you may prove another Guoliang!"

sentences.zh: 三月，抵上海，立開字營，凡千人，最為勁旅。

translations.literal: In the third month he reached Shanghai, formed the Kaizi Battalion of one thousand men in all—the hardest-fighting unit.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he arrived at Shanghai, organized the Kaizi Battalion of a thousand men—the crack force of the army.

sentences.zh: 屯虹橋，賊猝至，敗之。

translations.literal: He encamped at Hongqiao; the rebels came suddenly and he defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He encamped at Hongqiao; when rebels struck without warning, he beat them back.

sentences.zh: 次日又至，擊退，追至七里堡，大破之，會諸軍克南鎮橋。

translations.literal: The next day they came again; he repulsed them, pursued to Qilibao, and routed them utterly; joining the other armies he took Nanzhen Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: They returned the next day; he drove them off, pursued to Qilibao and inflicted a crushing defeat, then joined the allied columns in capturing Nanzhen Bridge.

sentences.zh: 五月，從鴻章援松江，軍於泗涇，賊酋陳炳文糾悍黨突營，分股繞攻上海，學啟營被圍，力禦，斃賊無算，仍不退。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he followed Hongzhang to relieve Songjiang and encamped at Sijing; the rebel chief Chen Bingwen gathered fierce bands to storm the camp, while detachments circled to attack Shanghai. Xueqi's camp was surrounded; he defended with force, killing rebels beyond count, yet they did not withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he marched with Hongzhang to relieve Songjiang and camped at Sijing. The rebel leader Chen Bingwen rallied hardened fighters for a surprise assault on the camp while other columns swung around to threaten Shanghai. Xueqi's battalion was encircled; he held firm and killed rebels beyond numbering, but the enemy would not pull back.

sentences.zh: 學啟開壁衝突，賊披靡，與諸軍夾攻，乃大潰。

translations.literal: Xueqi opened the stockade and charged out; the rebels scattered; with the other armies attacking from both sides, they were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Xueqi threw open the palisade and led a sortie; the rebels broke and fled, and with allied troops closing in from both flanks the enemy collapsed in complete rout.

sentences.zh: 松江圍解，擢副將，賜號勃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: The siege of Songjiang was lifted; he was promoted to brigadier general and granted the title Boyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: The siege of Songjiang was raised; he was promoted to deputy commander and honored with the title Boyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 進破賊於青浦東北，復其城。

translations.literal: Advancing, he defeated the rebels northeast of Qingpu and recovered the city.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced, routed the rebels northeast of Qingpu, and recovered the city.

sentences.zh: 八月，賊酋譚紹光由蘇州來犯，敗之七寶鎮，進戰北新涇，平其壘數十，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the rebel chief Tan Shaoguang came from Suzhou to attack; he defeated him at Qibao Town, advanced to fight at Beixinjing, leveled several tens of forts, and was entered on the rolls as major general.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the rebel commander Tan Shaoguang marched out from Suzhou; Xueqi defeated him at Qibao, fought on at Beixinjing, and leveled dozens of rebel stockades, earning nomination to the rank of major general.

sentences.zh: 九月，紹光復大舉窺上海，圍水陸各營於四江口，學啟會諸軍進擊，賊扼橋布陣。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Shaoguang again made a major move against Shanghai, besieging the land and river camps at Sikou; Xueqi joined the armies in attack, but the rebels held the bridge and deployed their formation.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Shaoguang launched another major thrust toward Shanghai and hemmed in the land and naval camps at Sikou. Xueqi united with the allied forces in a counterattack, but the rebels held the bridge and formed their battle line.

sentences.zh: 學啟陷陣，截斷賊隊，胸受砲傷，裹創疾鬥，賊卻走，未渡河者悉殲之。

translations.literal: Xueqi plunged into the formation, cut off the rebel column, took a cannon wound in the chest, bound the wound and fought on swiftly; the rebels retreated, and those who had not crossed the river were all annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Xueqi charged into the enemy line, severed the rebel column, and took a cannonball in the chest; he bound the wound and kept fighting. The rebels fell back, and every man who had not yet crossed the river was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 三路圍擊，殲斃落水者數万，盡毀賊營，以總兵記名加提督銜，授江西南贛鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Attacking from three routes in encirclement, tens of thousands were killed or drowned; all rebel camps were destroyed; he was entered as major general with the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief and appointed commander of the Nangan Garrison in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: A three-pronged encirclement killed or drowned rebels by the tens of thousands and destroyed every rebel camp. He was nominated major general with the honorary title of provincial military governor and appointed commander of the Nangan Garrison in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 自虹橋、泗涇、四江口三捷，皆以少擊眾，於是增軍至三千人。

translations.literal: From the three victories at Hongqiao, Sijing, and Sikou, in each he had struck the many with the few; his force was then increased to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongqiao, Sijing, and Sikou he had won three victories in succession, each time defeating larger forces with fewer troops; his command was accordingly expanded to three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 二年，進規蘇州，偕鴻章弟鶴章及英將戈登克太倉，賊酋蔡元隆詐降，擊殲之。

translations.literal: In the second year he advanced against Suzhou; together with Hongzhang's younger brother Hezhang and the English general Gordon he took Taicang; the rebel chief Cai Yuanlong feigned surrender and was attacked and annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tongzhi he pressed the campaign against Suzhou. Alongside Hongzhang's brother Hezhang and the British officer Gordon he captured Taicang; when the rebel leader Cai Yuanlong pretended to surrender, they attacked and destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 鴻章令學啟總統諸軍，學啟曰：「崑山三面阻水，一面陸路達蘇州，先斷其陸，乃可克。」

translations.literal: Hongzhang ordered Xueqi to command all the armies; Xueqi said: "Kunshan is blocked by water on three sides; one land route reaches Suzhou—first cut the land route, then it can be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang placed Xueqi in overall command of the forces. Xueqi said, "Kunshan is penned in by water on three sides, with only one land corridor to Suzhou—we must sever that corridor first, or the city cannot be taken."

sentences.zh: 偕郭松林破蘇州援賊於正儀鎮，遂克崑山，以提督記名，予一品封典。

translations.literal: Together with Guo Songlin he defeated Suzhou's relief rebels at Zhengyi Town, then took Kunshan; he was entered as provincial commander-in-chief and granted a first-rank patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: With Guo Songlin he routed Suzhou's relief force at Zhengyi, then captured Kunshan. He was nominated provincial military governor and granted a first-rank patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 連拔花涇、同里，克吳江。

translations.literal: In succession he captured Huajing and Tongli and took Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He took Huajing and Tongli in succession, then captured Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 賊憑太湖結寨，學啟扼飛虹橋，殲其酋徐尚友，乘勝破湖賊，悉平洞庭東山諸壘。

translations.literal: The rebels relied on Taihu to build stockades; Xueqi held Feihong Bridge, destroyed their chief Xu Shangyou, followed victory to break the lake rebels, and leveled all the forts of Dongshan on Lake Dongting.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had fortified themselves along Lake Tai; Xueqi seized Feihong Bridge, killed their leader Xu Shangyou, pressed the advantage against the lake forces, and cleared every rebel stronghold on Dongshan in the Dongting region.

sentences.zh: 七月，直抵蘇州婁門外永定橋駐軍。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he marched straight to Yongding Bridge outside Suzhou's Lou Gate and encamped.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he advanced directly to Yongding Bridge outside Suzhou's Lou Gate and made camp.

sentences.zh: 蘇州城大，四面阻水，寶帶橋為太湖鎖鑰，賊死力爭拒，合水陸軍大破之，平其壘，親督軍扼守。

translations.literal: Suzhou city was large, blocked by water on four sides; Baodai Bridge was the key to Taihu; the rebels contested with their lives; land and river armies together routed them utterly, leveled their forts, and he personally directed the troops in holding the position.
translations.idiomatic: Suzhou was a great walled city ringed by water on every side. Baodai Bridge was the strategic lock on Lake Tai, and the rebels fought to the death to hold it. The combined land and naval forces broke them decisively, leveled their redoubts, and Xueqi personally supervised the garrison that sealed the crossing.

sentences.zh: 李秀成自江寧率眾來援，大戰竟日，擊走之。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng led troops from Jiangning to relieve the city; they fought all day and he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng marched from Nanjing with a relief army; after a full day of fierce fighting Xueqi drove him off.

sentences.zh: 城賊數万復來爭，亦擊退。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of rebels from the city came again to contest it and were also repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of rebels sallied from the city to contest the position again, and he repulsed them as well.

sentences.zh: 進破五龍橋賊壘，留營駐守，分兵破嘉、湖援賊於百龍橋、八坼，逐北至平望。

translations.literal: Advancing he broke the rebel fort at Wulong Bridge, left a camp to garrison it, divided forces to defeat Jiaxing and Huzhou relief rebels at Bailong Bridge and Bache, and pursued north to Pingwang.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and stormed the rebel stockade at Wulong Bridge, left a garrison in place, detached troops to rout the Jiaxing and Huzhou relief columns at Bailong Bridge and Bache, and pursued north as far as Pingwang.

sentences.zh: 十月，李秀成糾李侍賢同踞無錫以為援，為劉銘傳、李鶴章所綴，學啟督戰益急，連破賊於蠡口、黃埭，攻破滸墅關及十里亭、虎丘賊壘，於是蘇州之圍遂合。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Li Xiucheng gathered Li Shixian to hold Wuxi together as relief; Liu Mingchuan and Li Hezhang pinned them down; Xueqi directed battle ever more urgently, in succession defeated rebels at Likou and Huangdai, stormed Xushuguan and the forts at Shiliting and Tiger Hill, and thus the encirclement of Suzhou was complete.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Li Xiucheng joined Li Shixian in holding Wuxi as a relief base, but Liu Mingchuan and Li Hezhang tied them down. Xueqi pressed the fighting harder still, routing rebels in succession at Likou and Huangdai and storming Xushuguan together with the stockades at Shiliting and Tiger Hill, until the ring around Suzhou closed tight.

sentences.zh: 賊自槃門至婁門連壘十餘裡，號曰「長城」，亦悉破。

translations.literal: The rebels from Pan Gate to Lou Gate had linked forts for more than ten li, called the "Long Wall," and these too were all broken.
translations.idiomatic: From Pan Gate to Lou Gate the rebels had thrown up a continuous line of fortifications for more than ten li, which they called the "Great Wall"—and these too were smashed in turn.

sentences.zh: 秀成知不可為，又江寧被圍急，遂以城守付其黨譚紹光，自出走。

translations.literal: Xiucheng knew nothing could be done; moreover Jiangning was urgently besieged, so he entrusted defense of the city to his follower Tan Shaoguang and fled himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xiucheng saw the situation was hopeless, and with Nanjing itself under tightening siege he handed the defense of Suzhou to his lieutenant Tan Shaoguang and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 賊酋郜雲官與副將鄭國魁舊識，密介通款，學啟與國魁及戈登單舸見雲官於洋澄湖，令斬紹光為信。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Gao Yunguan was an old acquaintance of Deputy Commander Zheng Guokui and secretly brokered surrender terms; Xueqi, Guokui, and Gordon went in a single boat to meet Yunguan on Yangcheng Lake and demanded that Shaoguang be beheaded as proof.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel commander Gao Yunguan was an old friend of Deputy Commander Zheng Guokui and secretly opened negotiations. Xueqi, Guokui, and Gordon rowed out alone on Yangcheng Lake to meet Yunguan and insisted that Shaoguang be killed as proof of good faith.

sentences.zh: 秀成行三日，紹光會諸酋議事，雲官即座上殺之，開​​齊門降。

translations.literal: Three days after Xiucheng's departure, Shaoguang convened the chiefs to discuss affairs; Yunguan killed him on the spot at the council and opened Qi Gate in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Xiucheng left, Shaoguang called the chiefs together for a council; Yunguan struck him down at the table and opened Qi Gate to surrender.

sentences.zh: 明日，學啟入城，賊酋列名者八人，雲官外，曰伍貴文、汪安均、周文佳、範啟發、張大洲、汪懷武、汪有為，皆歃血為誓，然未薙發，乞總兵副將官職，署其眾為二十營，劃半城為屯。

translations.literal: The next day Xueqi entered the city; eight rebel chiefs were listed by name—besides Yunguan: Wu Guiwen, Wang Anjun, Zhou Wenjia, Fan Qifa, Zhang Dazhou, Wang Huaiwu, and Wang Youwei—all swore blood oaths, yet had not shaved their heads; they begged for major-general and deputy-commander posts, organized their followers into twenty battalions, and divided half the city for encampment.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Xueqi entered the city. Eight rebel leaders were named besides Yunguan: Wu Guiwen, Wang Anjun, Zhou Wenjia, Fan Qifa, Zhang Dazhou, Wang Huaiwu, and Wang Youwei. They all swore binding oaths in blood, but had not yet cut their queues; they petitioned for major-general and deputy-commander commissions, reorganized their men into twenty battalions, and demanded half the city as their cantonment.

sentences.zh: 學啟佯許，密請李鴻章誅之。

translations.literal: Xueqi pretended to agree and secretly asked Li Hongzhang to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Xueqi feigned assent and secretly urged Li Hongzhang to have them killed.

sentences.zh: 鴻章謂殺降不祥，且堅他賊死拒心，未決。

translations.literal: Hongzhang said that killing those who surrendered was inauspicious and would moreover harden other rebels' will to resist to the death; he did not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang argued that slaughtering men who had surrendered would be ill-omened and would only steel the resolve of rebels elsewhere to fight to the death; he could not bring himself to decide.

sentences.zh: 學啟曰：「今賊眾尚不下二十萬，多吾軍數倍，徒以戰敗畏死乞降，心故未服。

translations.literal: Xueqi said: "Now the rebel host is still no less than two hundred thousand, several times our army; they beg surrender only because they fear death after defeat—their hearts are not yet submissive.
translations.idiomatic: Xueqi replied, "The rebels still number at least two hundred thousand men—several times our strength. They are begging to surrender only because they lost and fear death; their hearts are not yet won.

sentences.zh: 分城而處，變在肘腋，何以善其後？」

translations.literal: Dividing the city to dwell in it—revolt at one's elbow and armpit—how can the aftermath be managed well?"
translations.idiomatic: If we split the city and let them camp inside it, trouble will be at our very elbow—how can we hope to manage what comes after?"

sentences.zh: 鴻章乃許之。

translations.literal: Hongzhang then consented.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhang at last gave his consent.

sentences.zh: 次日，諸酋出城謁鴻章，留宴軍中。

translations.literal: The next day the chiefs came out of the city to pay respects to Hongzhang and were detained for a banquet in camp.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the chiefs came out to pay their respects to Hongzhang and were kept for a feast in the military camp.

sentences.zh: 酒半，健卒百餘挺矛入，刺八人皆死。

translations.literal: When the wine was half finished, more than a hundred stalwart soldiers entered with spears raised and stabbed all eight to death.
translations.idiomatic: Midway through the banquet, more than a hundred picked soldiers burst in with spears and ran all eight men through.

sentences.zh: 學啟嚴陣入城，​​以雲官等首示眾眾曰：「八人反側，已伏誅矣！」

translations.literal: Xueqi entered the city in battle array, displayed the heads of Yunguan and the others to the masses, and said: "The eight were disloyal and have already been executed!"
translations.idiomatic: Xueqi marched into the city in tight formation, displayed the heads of Yunguan and his fellows to the crowd, and proclaimed, "These eight were treacherous and have already paid with their lives!"

sentences.zh: 賊黨驚擾，殺其悍者數百人，餘不問，分別遣留，皆帖服，蘇州平。

translations.literal: The rebel party was alarmed and thrown into disorder; several hundred of the fiercest were killed, the rest were not questioned, and they were separately sent away or retained—all submitted, and Suzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel rank and file panicked; several hundred of the most hardened fighters were put to death, while the rest were left unmolested, sorted out, and either dismissed or kept on—all of whom submitted, and Suzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 乘勝偕李朝斌水師克平望，复嘉善。

translations.literal: Following victory, together with Li Chaobin's naval force he took Pingwang and recovered Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the advantage, he joined Li Chaobin's river flotilla in capturing Pingwang and recovering Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 三年春，進規嘉興，薄城下，破西門、北門賊壘七，分兵克秋涇、吳涇、合歡橋諸賊壘，逼賊築砲台。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year he advanced against Jiaxing, pressed close under the walls, broke seven rebel forts at the west and north gates, divided forces to take the rebel forts at Qiujing, Wujing, and Hehuan Bridge, and pressed the rebels to build gun platforms.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year he moved against Jiaxing, closed on the walls, stormed seven rebel redoubts at the west and north gates, detached columns to seize the stockades at Qiujing, Wujing, and Hehuan Bridge, and forced the rebels to throw up gun emplacements.

sentences.zh: 賊自盛澤、新塍來援，皆擊走之，圍攻匝月，毀賊砲台二十餘。

translations.literal: Rebels came in relief from Shengze and Xincheng and were all driven off; the siege lasted a full month and more than twenty rebel gun platforms were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Relief columns from Shengze and Xincheng were beaten back, and after a month-long siege more than twenty rebel batteries were demolished.

sentences.zh: 發地雷，裂城百丈，揮軍肉薄而登，忽中槍貫腦，踣而復起，部將劉士奇繼之，遂克嘉興。

translations.literal: They fired land mines, splitting the wall for a hundred zhang; he waved the army to press close and scale the wall, suddenly took a shot through the brain, fell and rose again; his subordinate commander Liu Shiji followed up, and Jiaxing was taken.
translations.idiomatic: A mine was detonated, breaching a hundred zhang of wall; he led the troops in a close assault up the breach, was suddenly struck by a bullet through the brain, fell, and rose again. His brigade commander Liu Shiji pressed the attack, and Jiaxing fell.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，詔嘉其身受重傷，攻拔堅城，命安心醫治，頒賞珍品。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, an edict praised him for bearing grave wounds and storming a stout-walled city, ordered him to rest and receive medical care, and bestowed rare gifts.
translations.idiomatic: When news of the victory arrived, the throne commended him for taking grave wounds in the storming of a fortified city, ordered him to convalesce under medical care, and sent rare gifts in reward.

sentences.zh: 尋以創重卒於軍。

translations.literal: Before long, from the severity of his wounds, he died in camp.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he succumbed to his wounds in camp.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏陳其兩年之間，复江、浙名城十數，克蘇州為東南第一戰功。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized that within two years he had recovered more than ten famous cities of Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and that the capture of Suzhou was the foremost military achievement in the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized that in the space of two years Xueqi had recovered more than a dozen famous cities across Jiangsu and Zhejiang, and that the fall of Suzhou ranked as the greatest single feat of arms in the southeast.

sentences.zh: 優詔賜卹，稱其謀勇兼優，贈太子太保，特遣員賜祭一壇，安慶、蘇州、嘉興建專祠，諡忠烈，予騎都尉兼雲騎尉世職，又加恩予三等輕車都尉世職，並為三等男爵。

translations.literal: A gracious edict granted mourning favors, calling his stratagem and valor both excellent; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; an envoy was specially dispatched to offer one altar of sacrifice; dedicated shrines were built at Anqing, Suzhou, and Jiaxing; his posthumous title was Zhonglie; he was granted hereditary posts as Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, with added favor of third-rank Commandant of Light Chariots, and was also made a third-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict granted posthumous honors, praising the excellence of both his strategy and his courage. He was posthumously appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent; a special envoy was dispatched to perform the sacrificial rites; dedicated shrines were erected at Anqing, Suzhou, and Jiaxing; he received the posthumous name Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce); hereditary ranks as Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant were conferred, with an additional grant of third-rank Commandant of Light Chariots, and he was ennobled as a third-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 初學啟投誠時，妻子皆為賊殺，以弟子建勳嗣，襲爵。

translations.literal: When Xueqi first came over in surrender, his wife and children had all been killed by the rebels; his nephew Jianxun was made heir and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When Xueqi first defected, the rebels had killed his wife and children; his nephew Jianxun was adopted as heir and succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 何安泰，安徽舒城人。

translations.literal: He Antai was a native of Shucheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: He Antai came from Shucheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少為傭，陷賊，從學啟來歸，轉戰，無役不從。

translations.literal: In youth he was a hired laborer, fell among rebels, followed Xueqi in coming over, fought in many campaigns, and was in no battle but he followed.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he had worked as a hired hand, fell in with the rebels, and followed Xueqi when he defected; he fought in campaign after campaign and was present at every engagement.

sentences.zh: 積功至記名總兵，加提督銜。

translations.literal: By accumulated merit he reached nomination as major general with the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His accumulated service earned nomination as major general with the honorary title of provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 從攻嘉興，履冰薄城，躍登中槍，死之，贈太子少保，予騎都尉世職。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Jiaxing, he walked on ice close under the wall, leaped up to scale it, was struck by a shot, and died; he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the hereditary post of Cavalry Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Jiaxing he crossed the ice to the foot of the wall, sprang up to scale it, was shot, and killed. He was posthumously appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and granted the hereditary rank of Cavalry Commandant.

sentences.zh: 嘉興人哀之，為祠以祀。

translations.literal: The people of Jiaxing mourned him and built a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Jiaxing mourned him and erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 鄭國魁，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Zheng Guokui was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Guokui came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，兩江總督何桂清令募勇屯無錫高橋，桂清棄軍走，國魁從提督曾秉忠於上海。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng the Governor-General of the Two Jiangs He Guiqing ordered levies raised and encamped at Gaobridge in Wuxi; Guiqing abandoned the army and fled; Guokui followed the provincial commander-in-chief Zeng Bingzhong at Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Xianfeng (1860), Governor-General He Guiqing of the Two Jiangs ordered militia raised and posted at Gaobridge in Wuxi. When Guiqing abandoned his troops and fled, Guokui joined Provincial Commander Zeng Bingzhong at Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 初李鴻章督師江蘇，檄領親兵水師後營，四江口、崑山、寶帶橋諸戰，功皆最，累擢至副將。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang first directed operations in Jiangsu, he was ordered to command the rear battalion of the personal guard naval force; at Sikou, Kunshan, Baodai Bridge, and other battles his merit was always foremost, and he was repeatedly promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang first took command in Jiangsu, Guokui was ordered to lead the rear battalion of the personal guard river force. At Sikou, Kunshan, Baodai Bridge, and other engagements his contributions always ranked first, and he rose by stages to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 蘇州既合圍，郜雲官與譚紹光不協，國魁遣人說之降，從程學啟會雲官，許雲官等二品武職，折箭誓不殺降，雲官如約獻城。

translations.literal: Once Suzhou was fully encircled, Gao Yunguan was at odds with Tan Shaoguang; Guokui sent men to persuade him to surrender; following Cheng Xueqi he met Yunguan, promised Yunguan and others second-rank military posts, broke an arrow and swore not to kill those who surrendered; Yunguan surrendered the city as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzhou was fully invested, Gao Yunguan fell out with Tan Shaoguang. Guokui sent envoys to negotiate his surrender and, with Cheng Xueqi, met Yunguan on the lake. He promised Yunguan and his fellows second-rank military commissions, broke an arrow in oath not to harm those who surrendered, and Yunguan delivered the city as pledged.

sentences.zh: 國魁先往宣諭，次日，大軍始入。

translations.literal: Guokui went first to proclaim and instruct; the next day the main army entered.
translations.idiomatic: Guokui went in first to announce the terms; only the next day did the main army enter the city.

sentences.zh: 既而云官等駢誅，國魁涕泣不食，自謂負約，辭不居功，仍以總兵記名，賜號勃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Before long Yunguan and the others were executed together; Guokui wept, refused food, considered himself to have broken faith, declined to claim merit, was still entered as major general, and granted the title Boyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunguan and his companions were then put to death together, Guokui wept and would not eat, believing he had broken his oath. He refused any share of the credit, remained on the rolls as major general, and was granted the title Boyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 從克嘉興、江陰、常州，予一品封典。

translations.literal: Following the capture of Jiaxing, Jiangyin, and Changzhou, he was granted a first-rank patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the capture of Jiaxing, Jiangyin, and Changzhou and was granted a first-rank patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，從剿東捻，駐防山東嶧縣。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi he followed the campaign against the Eastern Nian and garrisoned Yixian in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Tongzhi (1866) he joined the campaign against the Eastern Nian and was posted to garrison Yixian in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 捻平，以提督記名。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified, he was entered as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian were suppressed, he was nominated provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，署天津鎮總兵。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign he served as acting commander of the Tianjin Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu reign he served as acting commander of the Tianjin Garrison.

sentences.zh: 卒，附祀學啟專祠，蘇州士民思其功，建祠祀之。

translations.literal: He died, was enshrined jointly in Xueqi's dedicated temple, and the gentry and people of Suzhou, mindful of his merit, built a shrine to sacrifice to him.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given a place in the shrine dedicated to Xueqi; the scholars and common people of Suzhou, remembering his service, erected a shrine in his honor.

sentences.zh: 劉銘傳，字省三，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Liu Mingchuan, styled Sheng San, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mingchuan, whose courtesy name was Sheng San, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 少有大志。

translations.literal: In youth he had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a youth he harbored great ambitions.

sentences.zh: 咸豐四年，粵匪陷廬州，鄉團築堡自衛。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels took Luzhou; local militia built forts for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Xianfeng (1854), when the Taiping rebels seized Luzhou, local militia threw up fortified stockades for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 其父惠世為他堡豪者所辱，銘傳年十八，追數里殺之，自是為諸團所推重。

translations.literal: His father Huishi was insulted by a strongman of another fort; Mingchuan at eighteen pursued him several li and killed him; from then on he was esteemed by all the militia groups.
translations.idiomatic: When a bully from a neighboring stockade humiliated his father Huishi, the eighteen-year-old Mingchuan pursued him for several li and killed him, and from that day forward the local militia held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 從官軍克六安，援壽州，獎敘千總。

translations.literal: Following the government army he captured Lu'an and relieved Shouzhou, and was rewarded with registration as company commander.
translations.idiomatic: He marched with the imperial forces to take Lu'an and relieve Shouzhou, and was rewarded with registration as a company commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章募淮軍援江蘇，銘傳率練勇從至上海，號銘字營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang raised the Huai Army to relieve Jiangsu; Mingchuan led trained braves following to Shanghai, styled the Mingzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi (1862), when Li Hongzhang raised the Huai Army to relieve Jiangsu, Mingchuan led his militia to Shanghai, where his unit became known as the Mingzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 招撫南匯降賊吳建瀛、劉玉林眾四千人，簡精銳隸其軍。

translations.literal: He recruited and pacified four thousand men of the surrendered rebels Wu Jianying and Liu Yulin of Nanhui, selected the elite, and placed them under his army.
translations.idiomatic: He took into service four thousand surrendered rebels under Wu Jianying and Liu Yulin from Nanhui, picked out the best fighters, and incorporated them into his command.

sentences.zh: 賊由川沙來犯，擊敗之，連克奉賢、金山衛，累功擢參將，賜號驃勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Rebels came from Chuansha to attack and were defeated; in succession he took Fengxian and Jinshanwei; by accumulated merit he was promoted to lieutenant colonel and granted the title Biaoyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels advanced from Chuansha he routed them, then captured Fengxian and Jinshanwei in succession. His accumulated merits earned promotion to colonel and the title Biaoyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 又破賊野雞墩、四江口，擢副將。

translations.literal: He again defeated rebels at Yejidun and Sikou and was promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: He also defeated the rebels at Yejidun and Sikou and was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 常熟守賊以城降，被圍。

translations.literal: The rebels defending Changshu surrendered the city and were besieged.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel garrison at Changshu surrendered the city, only to find themselves besieged in turn.

sentences.zh: 二年春，銘傳會諸軍克福山，大破賊，解常熟圍，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Mingchuan joined the armies in taking Fushan, routed the rebels utterly, lifted the siege of Changshu, and was entered as major general.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year he joined the allied columns in capturing Fushan, inflicted a crushing defeat on the rebels, and raised the siege of Changshu, earning nomination as major general.

sentences.zh: 進規江陰，楊厙為沿江要衝，悍賊堅守，銘傳會黃翼升水師進攻，賊由無錫、江陰兩路來援，迭受創退。

translations.literal: Advancing against Jiangyin, Yangshe was a key point along the river; fierce rebels held it stubbornly; Mingchuan joined Huang Yisheng's naval force in attack; rebels came in relief from Wuxi and Jiangyin by two routes and were repeatedly wounded and driven back.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the campaign against Jiangyin. Yangshe was a critical point on the river line, held stubbornly by hardened rebels. Mingchuan coordinated with Huang Yisheng's river flotilla in the assault; relief columns from Wuxi and Jiangyin were beaten back again and again.

sentences.zh: 李秀成糾眾十餘萬分水陸復來援，銘傳力戰敗之。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng gathered more than a hundred thousand men by land and water to relieve the city again; Mingchuan fought fiercely and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng rallied more than a hundred thousand men by land and river to relieve the city once more; Mingchuan fought them off in a hard-fought victory.

sentences.zh: 七月，乘勝攻江陰，擒斬二萬，克其城，以提督記名。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, following victory he attacked Jiangyin, captured and killed twenty thousand, took the city, and was entered as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he pressed the advantage, assaulted Jiangyin, killed or captured twenty thousand rebels, and took the city, earning nomination as provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 尋复無錫，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Before long he recovered Wuxi and was given the first-rank official's hat ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He soon recovered Wuxi and was awarded the first-rank official's hat knob.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，進攻常州，敗賊於奔牛鎮。

translations.literal: That winter he advanced against Changzhou and defeated rebels at Benniu Town.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he moved against Changzhou and routed the rebels at Benniu.

sentences.zh: 賊目邵小雙降，令扼丹陽。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Shao Xiaoshuang surrendered and was ordered to hold Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel officer Shao Xiaoshuang surrendered and was ordered to block the route at Danyang.

sentences.zh: 援賊以輪舟至，犯奔牛，以掣圍城之師，奮擊，破三十餘壘，毀其舟。

translations.literal: Relief rebels came in steam vessels, attacked Benniu to pin down the besieging army; he fought fiercely, broke more than thirty forts, and destroyed their boats.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces arrived in steam launches and struck at Benniu to draw off the besieging troops. Mingchuan counterattacked fiercely, stormed more than thirty stockades, and destroyed their vessels.

sentences.zh: 三年春，合圍，破闉而入，擒斬賊首陳坤書，克常州，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: In the spring of the third year the encirclement closed; the gate-towers were broken and they entered; the rebel chief Chen Kunshu was captured and beheaded; Changzhou was taken and the yellow riding jacket was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the siege closed tight; the outer works were breached and the city entered. The rebel leader Chen Kunshu was captured and executed, Changzhou fell, and Mingchuan was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 進屯句容，江寧尋下，餘黨擁洪福瑱踞廣德，會諸軍擊走之。

translations.literal: Advancing he encamped at Jurong; Jiangning was soon taken; remnant factions supported Hong Futian in holding Guangde; joining the armies he drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and encamped at Jurong. Nanjing fell soon afterward, while remnant bands rallied around Hong Futian at Guangde; Mingchuan joined the allied forces and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 四年，曾國籓督師剿捻匪，主用淮軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zeng Guofan directed operations against the Nian bandits, relying chiefly on the Huai Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year (1865) Zeng Guofan took command of operations against the Nian rebels, relying chiefly on the Huai Army.

sentences.zh: 淮軍自程學啟歿後，銘傳為諸將冠。

translations.literal: After Cheng Xueqi's death the Huai Army had Mingchuan as foremost among its generals.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng Xueqi's death, Mingchuan stood at the head of the Huai Army's commanders.

sentences.zh: 調駐濟寧，尋分重兵為四鎮。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Jining; before long heavy forces were divided into four garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison Jining, and soon the main forces were split into four regional commands.

sentences.zh: 銘傳移駐周家口，迭破賊瓦店、南頓、扶溝，改為移擊之師，擢直隸提督。

translations.literal: Mingchuan moved his station to Zhoujiakou, in succession defeated rebels at Wadian, Nandun, and Fugou, was converted into a mobile striking force, and was promoted to provincial commander-in-chief of Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan shifted his headquarters to Zhoujiakou, routed the rebels in succession at Wadian, Nandun, and Fugou, was reorganized as a mobile strike force, and was promoted to provincial military governor of Zhili.

sentences.zh: 援湖北，克黃陂，追賊至潁州，大敗之。

translations.literal: He relieved Hubei, took Huangpi, pursued rebels to Yingzhou, and defeated them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: He marched to relieve Hubei, captured Huangpi, pursued the rebels to Yingzhou, and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 銘傳建議平原追賊不能制其死命，乃築長堤，自河南至山東運河，驅賊沙河以南蹙之。

translations.literal: Mingchuan proposed that pursuing rebels on the plains could not control their lives to the end; he therefore built a long dike from Henan to the Shandong Grand Canal, driving rebels south of the Sha River to hem them in.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan argued that chasing the rebels across open country would never bring them to bay, and proposed building a long embankment from Henan to the Shandong section of the Grand Canal to drive them south of the Sha River and pen them in.

sentences.zh: 工甫竣，豫軍防地為賊所破，乃分軍追剿，破之於鉅野。

translations.literal: The work had just been completed when the Henan army's defensive sector was broken by rebels; he then divided forces to pursue and suppress them and defeated them at Juye.
translations.idiomatic: The embankment had scarcely been finished when rebels breached the Henan army's defensive line; he detached columns in pursuit and routed them at Juye.

sentences.zh: 捻酋張總愚竄陝西，任柱、賴文光留山東，自此分為東西。

translations.literal: The Nian chief Zhang Zongyu fled into Shaanxi; Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang remained in Shandong; from then on they were divided into eastern and western groups.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian leader Zhang Zongyu broke west into Shaanxi, while Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang remained in Shandong, and from that point the movement split into eastern and western wings.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章代國籓督師，銘傳專剿東捻，東至鄆城，西至京山，大小數十戰。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang replaced Guofan in directing operations; Mingchuan specialized in suppressing the Eastern Nian, from Yuncheng in the east to Jingshan in the west, fighting several tens of battles large and small.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang replaced Guofan as supreme commander, Mingchuan took charge of operations against the Eastern Nian, campaigning from Yuncheng in the east to Jingshan in the west in several dozen engagements large and small.

sentences.zh: 六年春，賊走尹隆河，與鮑超約期會擊。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year the rebels fled to the Yinlong River; he arranged a date with Bao Chao for a joint attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year the rebels retreated toward the Yinlong River, and Mingchuan arranged a coordinated strike with Bao Chao.

sentences.zh: 銘傳先期至，戰失利，部將唐殿魁死之。

translations.literal: Mingchuan arrived ahead of schedule; the battle went badly; his subordinate commander Tang Diankui was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan reached the rendezvous early, but the engagement went against him and his brigade commander Tang Diankui was killed.

sentences.zh: 休屯信陽，整軍復進，追賊至山東。

translations.literal: He rested and encamped at Xinyang, reorganized the army and advanced again, pursuing rebels into Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: He halted at Xinyang to regroup, then marched again in pursuit of the rebels into Shandong.

sentences.zh: 复議自運河至膠、萊，長圍困賊，杜其西趨。

translations.literal: He again proposed a long encirclement from the Grand Canal to Jiao and Lai to trap the rebels and block their westward flight.
translations.idiomatic: He renewed his proposal for a long encirclement from the Grand Canal to the Jiao and Lai peninsula to pen the rebels in and cut off their escape westward.

sentences.zh: 時兵、賊俱疲，朝命督戰益急，鴻章專倚銘傳。

translations.literal: At the time both army and rebels were exhausted; court orders to press battle grew ever more urgent; Hongzhang relied on Mingchuan alone.
translations.idiomatic: Both armies were by then exhausted, yet the court pressed ever harder for results; Hongzhang placed his sole reliance on Mingchuan.

sentences.zh: 八月，解沭陽圍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he lifted the siege of Shuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he raised the siege of Shuyang.

sentences.zh: 戰贛榆，購降賊內應，槍斃任柱於陣，賊大潰。

translations.literal: Fighting at Ganyu, he bought surrendered rebels as inside collaborators; Ren Zhu was shot dead on the field; the rebels were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: At Ganyu he bribed defectors to act as agents within the enemy ranks; Ren Zhu was gunned down in battle and the rebel army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 邀擊濰縣、壽光，薄之洋河、瀰河之間，殲賊幾盡。

translations.literal: He intercepted them at Weixian and Shouguang, pressed them between the Yang and Mi rivers, and annihilated the rebels almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: He intercepted the fleeing columns at Weixian and Shouguang, cornered them between the Yang and Mi rivers, and all but wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 賴文光走揚州就擒，東捻遂平。

translations.literal: Lai Wenguang fled to Yangzhou and was captured; the Eastern Nian were thus pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Wenguang fled to Yangzhou and was taken prisoner, and the Eastern Nian rebellion was at last suppressed.

sentences.zh: 國籓、鴻章奏捷，論銘傳為首功，予三等輕車都尉世職。

translations.literal: Guofan and Hongzhang reported victory; Mingchuan was judged to have the foremost merit and was granted the hereditary post of third-rank Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan and Hongzhang memorialized the victory, crediting Mingchuan with the leading share of the merit and conferring the hereditary rank of third-rank Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 以積勞致疾，乞假去軍。

translations.literal: From accumulated toil he fell ill and begged leave to leave the army.
translations.idiomatic: Worn down by years of campaigning, he fell ill and requested leave to retire from active service.

sentences.zh: 七年春，張總愚突犯畿輔，急起銘傳赴援，以遲緩被譴責。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year Zhang Zongyu suddenly invaded the capital region; Mingchuan was urgently recalled to relieve the crisis but was censured for slowness.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year Zhang Zongyu suddenly struck into the metropolitan region; Mingchuan was urgently recalled to the rescue but was rebuked for his delay.

sentences.zh: 及至東昌，會諸軍進剿鹽山、滄州、德平，仍用長圍策，蹙之運河東，縱橫合擊，殲賊殆盡，總愚走茌平，陷水死。

translations.literal: When he reached Dongchang he joined the armies in advancing against Yanshan, Cangzhou, and Dezhou, still using the long-encirclement strategy, pressing them east of the Grand Canal; attacking from all sides in concert, the rebels were almost all annihilated; Zongyu fled to Chiping and drowned in the water.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he reached Dongchang he had joined the allied columns in operations against Yanshan, Cangzhou, and Dezhou. Again employing the long encirclement strategy, he drove the rebels east of the Grand Canal and closed in from every direction until they were nearly exterminated. Zongyu fled to Chiping and drowned.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，錫封一等男爵。

translations.literal: When the Western Nian were pacified, he was enfeoffed as a first-rank baron.
translations.idiomatic: With the Western Nian suppressed, he was ennobled as a first-rank baron.

sentences.zh: 詔屯張秋，九月，命督辦陝西軍務。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to garrison Zhangqiu; in the ninth month he was appointed to supervise military affairs in Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to garrison Zhangqiu, and in the ninth month was appointed to direct military operations in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 率唐定奎、滕學義、黃桂蘭等搜剿北山回匪，疏陳大勢，引病乞罷，歸里。

translations.literal: Leading Tang Dingkui, Teng Xueyi, Huang Guilan, and others he searched out and suppressed Hui bandits in the northern hills; he memorialized on the overall situation, cited illness to beg dismissal, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He led Tang Dingkui, Teng Xueyi, Huang Guilan, and others in operations against Hui rebels in the northern hills, submitted a memorial on the strategic situation, pleaded illness to resign, and returned to his native place.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，俄羅斯議還伊犁，有違言，急備邊。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu Russia negotiated the return of Ili but there were words of breach; border defense was urgently prepared.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Guangxu, when Russia was negotiating the return of Ili but talk of a breach arose, the frontier defenses were urgently strengthened.

sentences.zh: 召銘傳至京，疏陳兵事，略謂：「練兵造器，固宜次第舉行，其機括則在鐵路。

translations.literal: Mingchuan was summoned to the capital; he memorialized on military affairs, saying in summary: "Training troops and manufacturing weapons should indeed be carried out in due order, but the pivot lies in railways.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchuan was summoned to Beijing and memorialized on military affairs, arguing in essence: "Drilling troops and manufacturing arms should certainly proceed step by step, but the key lies in railways.

sentences.zh: 鐵路之利，不可殫述，於用兵尤為急不可緩。

translations.literal: The benefits of railways cannot be fully enumerated; for military use they are especially urgent and cannot be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: The advantages of railways are beyond full enumeration, and for military purposes they are a matter that brooks no delay.

sentences.zh: 中國幅員遼闊，防不勝防，鐵路一開，南北東西呼吸相通，無徵調倉皇之慮，無轉輸艱阻之虞，從此裁兵節餉，並成勁旅，一兵可得十兵之用。

translations.literal: China's territory is vast and wide; defense cannot defend everywhere; once railways are opened, north, south, east, and west breathe in communication; there is no worry of hurried mobilization, no fear of difficult transport; from this one may cut troops and save pay, form crack armies together, and one soldier may serve the use of ten.
translations.idiomatic: China's territory is vast beyond guarding everywhere at once. Once railways are built, the four directions will be linked as if in a single breath: no more frantic last-minute mobilizations, no more crippling transport bottlenecks. Troops could then be reduced and pay saved while elite forces were consolidated, so that one soldier might do the work of ten.

sentences.zh: 權操自上，不為疆臣所牽制，立自強之基礎，杜外人之覬覦，胥在於此。」

translations.literal: Power would be wielded from above, not constrained by frontier officials; the foundation of self-strengthening would be laid and foreigners' covetous glances blocked—all in this."
translations.idiomatic: Central authority would hold the reins, unhampered by provincial strongmen; the foundation of national self-strengthening would be laid and foreign encroachment checked—all of this hinged on railways."

sentences.zh: 疏上，雖格未行，中國鐵路之興，實自銘傳發之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; though rejected and not implemented, China's rise of railways in fact began from Mingchuan's initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Though the memorial was set aside and not adopted, the movement to build railways in China in fact originated with Mingchuan.

sentences.zh: 十一年，法蘭西兵擾粵、閩，詔起銘傳，加巡撫銜，督台灣軍務。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year French troops harassed Guangdong and Fujian; an edict recalled Mingchuan, gave him the brevet rank of governor, and put him in charge of Taiwan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year French forces threatened Guangdong and Fujian; Mingchuan was recalled to service, granted the brevet rank of governor, and placed in command of Taiwan's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 條上海防武備十事，多被採行。

translations.literal: He listed ten items on coastal defense and military preparedness; many were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten proposals on coastal defense and armaments, most of which were adopted.

sentences.zh: 抵台灣未一月，法兵至，毀基隆砲台，銘傳以無兵艦不能海戰，伺登陸，戰於山後，殲敵百餘人，斃其三酋，復基隆，而終不能守。

translations.literal: Less than a month after reaching Taiwan, French troops arrived, destroyed the Keelung batteries; Mingchuan, having no warships and unable to fight at sea, waited for them to land, fought behind the hills, annihilated more than a hundred of the enemy and killed three of their chiefs, recovered Keelung, yet in the end could not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month of his arrival in Taiwan the French landed and destroyed the Keelung batteries. Without warships Mingchuan could not contest the sea; he waited for the enemy to come ashore and fought them in the hills behind the port, killing more than a hundred French troops and three of their officers, and briefly retook Keelung—but could not hold it in the end.

sentences.zh: 扼滬尾，調江南兵艦，阻不得達。

translations.literal: He held Huwei; Jiangnan warships were ordered up but could not get through.
translations.idiomatic: He held the line at Huwei and called for warships from Jiangnan, but they could not break through the blockade.

sentences.zh: 敵三犯滬尾，又犯月眉山，皆擊退，殲敵千餘，相持八閱月。

translations.literal: The enemy thrice attacked Huwei and also attacked Yuemei Hill; all were repulsed; more than a thousand of the enemy were annihilated; the standoff lasted eight months.
translations.idiomatic: The French attacked Huwei three times and also struck at Yuemei Hill; Mingchuan beat them back each time, killing more than a thousand of the enemy, and the two sides remained locked in stalemate for eight months.

sentences.zh: 十一年，和議成，法兵始退。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year peace was concluded and the French troops withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year a peace settlement was reached and the French withdrew.

sentences.zh: 初授福建巡撫，尋改台灣為行省，改台灣巡撫。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed Governor of Fujian; soon Taiwan was made a province and he was made Governor of Taiwan.
translations.idiomatic: He was first appointed governor of Fujian; soon afterward Taiwan was elevated to provincial status and he became its governor.

sentences.zh: 增改郡、廳、州、縣，改澎湖協為鎮，檄將吏入山剿撫南、中、北三路，前後山生番，薙發歸化。

translations.literal: He added and revised prefectures, sub-prefectures, departments, and counties; converted the Penghu Brigade into a Garrison; ordered officers into the mountains to suppress and pacify the southern, central, and northern routes; the raw tribes of the front and rear mountains shaved their heads and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He reorganized the administrative divisions, elevated the Penghu garrison command, and dispatched officers into the mountains to pacify the aboriginal peoples of the southern, central, and northern routes. The hill tribes of eastern and western Taiwan cut their queues and accepted Qing rule.

sentences.zh: 丈田清賦，溢舊額三十六萬兩有奇，增茶、鹽、金、煤、林木諸稅。

translations.literal: He measured fields and cleared tax registers, exceeding the old quota by more than three hundred and sixty thousand taels; he increased taxes on tea, salt, gold, coal, timber, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He conducted a land survey and cleaned up the tax registers, raising revenue more than three hundred and sixty thousand taels above the old quota, and introduced new levies on tea, salt, gold, coal, timber, and other resources.

sentences.zh: 始至，歲入九十餘萬，後增至三百萬。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, annual revenue was more than nine hundred thousand; later it rose to three million.
translations.idiomatic: Annual revenue stood at just over nine hundred thousand taels when he arrived; by the end of his tenure it had risen to three million.

sentences.zh: 築砲台，興造鐵路、電線，防務差具。

translations.literal: He built batteries, undertook railways and telegraph lines, and coastal defense was roughly in place.
translations.idiomatic: He constructed fortifications, promoted railways and telegraph lines, and brought Taiwan's defenses to a workable state.

sentences.zh: 加太子少保。

translations.literal: He was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十六年，加兵部尚書銜，命幫辦海軍事務。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was given the brevet rank of Minister of War and ordered to assist in naval affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was granted the brevet rank of Minister of War and assigned to assist in naval affairs.

sentences.zh: 屢因病陳請乞罷，久始允之。

translations.literal: Repeatedly citing illness he memorialized to beg dismissal; only after a long time was this granted.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly pleaded illness and asked to resign; only after a long delay was his request granted.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，朝鮮兵事起，屢召，以病未出。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the Korean military crisis arose; he was repeatedly summoned but did not go out because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year war broke out in Korea; he was summoned repeatedly but did not take the field, pleading illness.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，詔念前功，贈太子太保，賜卹，建專祠，諡壯肅。

translations.literal: Before long he died; an edict recalled his former merit; he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted mourning favors, given a dedicated shrine, and given the posthumous title Zhuangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward. The throne remembered his past service, posthumously appointed him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted mourning honors, erected a dedicated shrine, and gave him the posthumous name Zhuangsu (Stalwart and Stern).

sentences.zh: 張樹珊，字海柯，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Zhang Shushan, styled Haige, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shushan, whose courtesy name was Haige, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪入安徽，樹珊與兄樹聲練鄉兵自衛，淮軍之興，自張氏始。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels entered Anhui; Shushan and his elder brother Shusheng trained local militia for self-defense; the rise of the Huai Army began with the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, when the Taiping rebels invaded Anhui, Shushan and his elder brother Shusheng organized local militia for self-defense—the origins of the Huai Army lay with the Zhang family.

sentences.zh: 五年，擊賊巢湖，率壯士數十人敗賊，擒斬賊目五人，進破巢縣賊營，敘外委。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he attacked rebels at Chaohu, led several tens of stalwarts to defeat the rebels, captured and beheaded five rebel officers, advanced to break the rebel camp at Chaoxian, and was registered as an external commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fought rebels at Lake Chaohu, led a few dozen picked men to rout them, captured and beheaded five rebel officers, stormed the rebel camp at Chaoxian, and was registered as an external commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，復來安，隨官軍克無為州，擢千總。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he recovered Lai'an, followed the government army in taking Wuwei Prefecture, and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he recovered Lai'an, marched with the imperial forces to take Wuwei, and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 又克潛山，至太湖，遇賊數万，樹珊僅五百人，軍糧火藥皆盡。

translations.literal: He also took Qianshan; reaching Taihu he met tens of thousands of rebels; Shushan had only five hundred men; army grain and gunpowder were all exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Qianshan, but at Lake Taihu he ran into tens of thousands of rebels while he had only five hundred men and his supplies of food and gunpowder were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 賊屯堤上，樹珊選死士緣堤下蛇行入賊中，大呼擊殺，賊驚潰。

translations.literal: The rebels encamped on the dike; Shushan selected death-dedicated soldiers to crawl like snakes along the foot of the dike into the rebels, shouted and struck to kill; the rebels were alarmed and routed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were camped atop the dike; Shushan picked volunteers to crawl along its base into the enemy ranks, then sprang up shouting and slashing. The rebels panicked and fled.

sentences.zh: 七年，敗捻首張洛行於官亭。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he defeated the Nian chief Zhang Luoxing at Guanting.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he defeated the Nian leader Zhang Luoxing at Guanting.

sentences.zh: 粵匪方與捻相勾結，皖北幾無完區，獨合肥西鄉以團練築堡差安，時出境從勦賊。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels were then in league with the Nian; north Anhui had almost no intact districts; only the western townships of Hefei, with militia building forts, were somewhat secure, and from time to time crossed the border to join in suppressing rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebels were then in league with the Nian, and almost no part of northern Anhui remained intact. Only the western townships of Hefei, where militia had thrown up fortified stockades, enjoyed relative security, and from time to time sent men across the border to join government campaigns.

sentences.zh: 九年，克霍山。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he took Huoshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he captured Huoshan.

sentences.zh: 十年，兩解六安圍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he twice lifted the siege of Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he twice raised the siege of Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 十一年，赴援壽州，克三河，擢都司，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went to relieve Shouzhou, took Sanhe, was promoted to battalion commander, and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he marched to relieve Shouzhou, captured Sanhe, was promoted to battalion commander, and awarded the peacock feather insignia.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從李鴻章赴上海，名其軍曰樹字營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai and named his army the Shuzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, where his unit became known as the Shuzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 李秀成犯上海，會諸軍夾擊走之。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng attacked Shanghai; joining the armies he attacked from both sides and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiucheng threatened Shanghai, Shushan joined the allied forces in a pincer attack and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 七月，會克青浦。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he joined in taking Qingpu.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he took part in the capture of Qingpu.

sentences.zh: 賊圍北新涇，樹珊偕程學啟力戰旬餘，賊始遁，擢游擊。

translations.literal: Rebels besieged Beixinjing; Shushan together with Cheng Xueqi fought fiercely for more than ten days before the rebels fled; he was promoted to acting major.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels besieged Beixinjing, Shushan fought alongside Cheng Xueqi for more than ten days until the enemy withdrew, and was promoted to brevet major.

sentences.zh: 進克嘉定，賊大舉圍四江口，樹珊偪賊而營，會諸軍奮擊，連破二十餘壘，遂解圍，擢參將，賜號悍勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Advancing he took Jiading; rebels made a major move to besiege Sikou; Shushan pressed close to the rebels in camp; joining the armies in fierce attack he broke more than twenty forts in succession and lifted the siege; he was promoted to lieutenant colonel and granted the title Hanyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and captured Jiading. When rebels launched a major assault on Sikou, Shushan pitched camp close against the enemy line, joined the allied forces in a furious attack, stormed more than twenty stockades in succession, and raised the siege. He was promoted to colonel and granted the title Hanyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，常熟及福山賊以城降，而福山賊复叛，圍常熟。

translations.literal: That winter the rebels of Changshu and Fushan surrendered their cities, but the Fushan rebels rebelled again and besieged Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the rebel garrisons at Changshu and Fushan surrendered their cities, but the Fushan force rebelled again and laid siege to Changshu.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，樹珊率軍航海抵福山西洋港，風潮作，飄舟近賊巢，潮退不得行。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Shushan led his army by sea to Xiyang Harbor at Fushan; wind and tide rose, the boats drifted near the rebel nest, and when the tide fell they could not move.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the second year Shushan led his troops by sea to Xiyang Harbor near Fushan. A storm drove his boats aground near the rebel stronghold, and when the tide fell they were stranded.

sentences.zh: 樹珊曰：「兵法危地則戰。」

translations.literal: Shushan said: "In military law, in perilous ground one fights."
translations.idiomatic: Shushan said, "The art of war teaches that in desperate ground one must fight."

sentences.zh: 登岸結壘未就，賊大至，樹珊疾搗中堅，槍傷左肘不少卻，拔出諸營之被圍者，進解常熟之圍，擢副將。

translations.literal: He went ashore; before the fort was finished the rebels came in force; Shushan swiftly struck their center; a gunshot wounded his left elbow but he did not retreat much; he extricated the encircled camps, advanced to lift the siege of Changshu, and was promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: He went ashore and began throwing up a stockade before it was half finished the rebels swarmed in. Shushan charged straight at their center; a bullet struck his left elbow but he scarcely slowed, broke through to relieve the encircled camps, and raised the siege of Changshu. He was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 會諸軍進攻江陰，樹珊扼南門，斷賊去路，城复，賊無得脫者，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Joining the armies in the attack on Jiangyin, Shushan held the south gate, cut off the rebels' escape route; when the city was recovered none of the rebels could escape; he was entered as major general.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Jiangyin he sealed the south gate and cut off the rebels' escape. When the city fell, none got away, and he was nominated major general.

sentences.zh: 進攻無錫，悍酋陳坤書、李世賢方以十萬眾圍大橋角，樹珊助剿，火賊輪船二、砲船十，殲斃甚眾，解其圍。

translations.literal: Advancing against Wuxi, the fierce chiefs Chen Kunshu and Li Shixian were just then besieging Daqiaojiao with a hundred thousand men; Shushan assisted in suppression, burned two rebel steamers and ten gunboats, killed and annihilated a great many, and lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: In the advance on Wuxi, the hardened rebel commanders Chen Kunshu and Li Shixian had a hundred thousand men besieging Daqiaojiao. Shushan joined the relief effort, set fire to two rebel steamers and ten gunboats, killed a great many of the enemy, and broke the siege.

sentences.zh: 李秀成復率眾數万至，連營數十里，樹珊與諸軍夾擊，賊大潰。

translations.literal: Li Xiucheng again led several tens of thousands of men; they linked camps for several tens of li; Shushan with the armies attacked from both sides and the rebels were utterly routed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiucheng returned with tens of thousands of men and pitched a camp line several li long; Shushan and the allied forces struck from both flanks and routed them completely.

sentences.zh: 會蘇州已下，秀成率死黨入太湖，結常州賊，水陸分進，援無錫；

translations.literal: Suzhou had already fallen; Xiucheng led diehard followers into Taihu, joined with the Changzhou rebels, advanced by land and water in division to relieve Wuxi;
translations.idiomatic: By then Suzhou had fallen; Xiucheng led his diehard followers into Lake Taihu, linked up with the Changzhou rebels, and advanced by land and river in separate columns to relieve Wuxi;

sentences.zh: 時銘傳專擊外援賊，樹珊與諸軍合圍，十一月，拔之，以提督記名。

translations.literal: at the time Mingchuan specialized in striking relief rebels; Shushan with the armies completed the encirclement; in the eleventh month it was taken; he was entered as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: while Mingchuan concentrated on the relief columns. Shushan and the allied armies closed the ring; in the eleventh month Wuxi fell, and he was nominated provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 偕兄樹聲及劉銘傳進攻常州，三年四月，克之，予一品封典，授廣西右江鎮總兵。

translations.literal: Together with his elder brother Shusheng and Liu Mingchuan he advanced against Changzhou; in the fourth month of the third year it was taken; he was granted a first-rank patent of nobility and appointed commander of the Youjiang Garrison in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Alongside his brother Shusheng and Liu Mingchuan he pressed the attack on Changzhou, which fell in the fourth month of the third year. He received a first-rank patent of nobility and appointment as commander of the Youjiang Garrison in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 四年，曾國籓督師剿捻，駐徐州，以樹珊所部為親軍，令援山東，破賊於魚台。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Zeng Guofan directed operations against the Nian, encamped at Xuzhou, took Shushan's command as his personal guard, ordered relief of Shandong, and defeated rebels at Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zeng Guofan took command of anti-Nian operations and encamped at Xuzhou, keeping Shushan's troops as his personal guard. Shushan was sent to relieve Shandong and defeated the rebels at Yutai.

sentences.zh: 議設四鎮，陳州之周家口為最要，初以劉銘傳駐之，既改銘傳為游擊之師，乃令樹珊移駐。

translations.literal: Four garrisons were proposed; Zhoujiakou in Chenzhou was the most critical; at first Liu Mingchuan was stationed there; once Mingchuan was converted to a mobile striking force, Shushan was ordered to move his garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: Four regional commands were established, with Zhoujiakou in Chenzhou as the most critical post. Liu Mingchuan was first stationed there; when his force was reorganized as a mobile strike column, Shushan was ordered to take his place.

sentences.zh: 五年三月，擊賊沙河，賊竄撲周家口，回軍夾擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the third month of the fifth year he struck rebels at the Sha River; rebels fled and struck at Zhoujiakou; he turned his army and attacked from both sides to defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the fifth year he fought the rebels along the Sha River; when they doubled back to strike Zhoujiakou, he wheeled his force and crushed them in a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 五月，又敗賊於沙河東，樹珊以賊騎飄勿靡常，恥株守，請改為游擊之師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he again defeated rebels east of the Sha River; Shushan, because rebel cavalry drifted without fixed pattern, was ashamed of static defense, and requested conversion to a mobile striking force.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he routed the rebels again east of the Sha River. Shushan, finding static garrison duty ill-suited to the Nian cavalry's elusive tactics, asked that his command be reorganized as a mobile strike force.

sentences.zh: 九月，馳解許州之圍。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he rushed to lift the siege of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he raced to raise the siege of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十月，逐賊山東境，連敗之豐南、定陶、曹縣。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he pursued rebels into Shandong territory and in succession defeated them at Fengnan, Dingtao, and Caoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he pursued the rebels into Shandong and routed them in succession at Fengnan, Dingtao, and Caoxian.

sentences.zh: 十一月，回軍周家口。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he returned his army to Zhoujiakou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he marched his army back to Zhoujiakou.

sentences.zh: 賊竄湖北，偕總兵周盛波追剿。

translations.literal: Rebels fled into Hubei; together with Major General Zhou Shengbo he pursued and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels broke into Hubei, he joined Major General Zhou Shengbo in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 會郭松林敗績於臼口，賊焰愈熾，樹珊自黃岡追至棗陽，賊竄黃州、德安，樹珊馳援。

translations.literal: Guo Songlin suffered defeat at Jiukou; rebel flames burned ever hotter; Shushan pursued from Huanggang to Zaoyang; rebels fled to Huangzhou and De'an; Shushan rushed to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Songlin was defeated at Jiukou the rebels' momentum surged. Shushan pursued from Huanggang to Zaoyang; when the rebels veered toward Huangzhou and De'an he raced to intercept.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆言賊悍且眾，宜持重，樹珊率親軍二百人窮追，抵新家徬。

translations.literal: All the generals said the rebels were fierce and numerous and one should be cautious; Shushan led two hundred men of his personal guard in relentless pursuit and reached Xinjia Bang.
translations.idiomatic: The other commanders urged caution against fierce and numerous rebels, but Shushan pressed on with two hundred men of his personal guard and caught up with the enemy at Xinjia Bang.

sentences.zh: 賊橫走抄官軍後，樹珊力戰陷陣，至夜半，馬立積尸中不能行，下馬鬥而死。

translations.literal: Rebels moved crosswise to outflank the government army's rear; Shushan fought fiercely and plunged into the formation; by midnight his horse stood amid piled corpses and could not move; he dismounted and fought to death.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels swung around to strike the imperial force from the rear. Shushan charged into the enemy line and fought on until midnight, when his horse could no longer move for the heaped corpses around it. He dismounted and fought on foot until he was killed.

sentences.zh: 後隊據鄉莊發槍砲拒賊，賊亦尋退，全軍未敗。

translations.literal: The rear column held a village and fired guns and cannon to repel the rebels; the rebels soon withdrew; the whole army was not defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The rearguard held a village and opened fire with muskets and cannon; the rebels soon withdrew, and the army as a whole was not broken.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔惜其忠勇，從優議卹，予騎都尉兼一云騎尉世職，建專祠，諡勇烈。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict lamented his loyalty and valor, granted mourning favors from the favorable scale, gave the hereditary posts of Cavalry Commandant and one Cloud Cavalry Commandant, built a dedicated shrine, and gave the posthumous title Yonglie.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an edict mourned his loyal courage, granted the highest posthumous honors, conferred hereditary ranks as Cavalry Commandant and Cloud Cavalry Commandant, erected a dedicated shrine, and gave him the posthumous name Yonglie (Brave and Fierce).

sentences.zh: 七年，捻平，加贈太子少保。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Nian were pacified, he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Nian were finally suppressed, he was posthumously appointed Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 弟樹屏，從諸兄治團練，積勞至千總。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shuping followed his elder brothers in managing militia training; by accumulated toil he reached company commander.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shuping had joined his elder brothers in organizing the militia and rose by accumulated service to company commander.

sentences.zh: 從樹珊至江蘇，轉戰松江、蘇州、常州，屢有功，累擢副將。

translations.literal: Following Shushan to Jiangsu, he fought at Songjiang, Suzhou, and Changzhou, had merit repeatedly, and was repeatedly promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shushan to Jiangsu and fought through Songjiang, Suzhou, and Changzhou with repeated distinction, rising by stages to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 從剿捻匪，迭破賊於豐縣、沛縣、魚台。

translations.literal: Following the suppression of Nian bandits, he in succession defeated rebels at Fengxian, Peixian, and Yutai.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against the Nian he routed the rebels in succession at Fengxian, Peixian, and Yutai.

sentences.zh: 及樹珊戰歿德安，樹屏分領樹字三營駐周家口。

translations.literal: When Shushan died in battle at De'an, Shuping took command of three battalions of the Shuzi force and garrisoned Zhoujiakou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shushan fell at De'an, Shuping took over three battalions of the Shuzi force and garrisoned Zhoujiakou.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，論功以提督記名，賜號額騰額巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Nian were pacified, his merit was judged and he was entered as provincial commander-in-chief and granted the title Eteng'e Batür.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Nian were suppressed, he was nominated provincial military governor and granted the title Eteng'e Batür.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，山西巡撫李宗羲奏調，令募新軍六營分駐大寧、吉州、壺口防回匪。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi the Governor of Shanxi Li Zongyi memorialized to transfer him, ordering him to raise six battalions of new troops to garrison separately at Daning, Jizhou, and Hukou against Hui bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tongzhi, Governor Li Zongyi of Shanxi requested his transfer and ordered him to raise six new battalions to garrison Daning, Jizhou, and Hukou against Hui rebels.

sentences.zh: 十二年，兼統水陸駐河津，分防歸化、包頭。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he also commanded land and river forces garrisoned at Hejin, with separate defense of Guihua and Baotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he took joint command of land and river forces at Hejin, with detachments guarding Guihua and Baotou.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，甘肅流賊犯河套後山，督軍追擊，連敗之，擒其渠曹洪照。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu Gansu roving bandits invaded the rear hills of the Hetao; he directed the army in pursuit, defeated them in succession, and captured their leader Cao Hongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu, when Gansu bandits raided the rear hills of the Hetao region, he led the pursuit, routed them in successive engagements, and captured their leader Cao Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 事平，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled, he was given the first-rank official's hat ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When the disturbance was quelled, he was awarded the first-rank official's hat knob.

sentences.zh: 四年，授太原鎮總兵，值旱災，樹屏捐運賑糧，出軍食之餘平糶濟饑民。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was appointed commander of the Taiyuan Garrison; a drought disaster occurred; Shuping donated transport of relief grain, and from army provisions beyond need sold grain at fair price to relieve the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was appointed commander of the Taiyuan Garrison. During a severe drought he donated grain for relief transport and sold army surplus rations at fair prices to feed the starving populace.

sentences.zh: 六年，移防包頭。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to garrison Baotou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to garrison Baotou.

sentences.zh: 九年，調大同鎮。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to the Datong Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was transferred to the Datong Garrison.

sentences.zh: 十三年，因傷病乞罷，十七年，卒，以前勞賜卹。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, citing wounds and illness he begged dismissal; in the seventeenth year he died and was granted mourning favors for former toil.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he resigned, citing wounds and illness; he died in the seventeenth year and was granted posthumous honors for his past service.

sentences.zh: 周盛波，字海舲，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Zhou Shengbo, styled Hailing, was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shengbo, whose courtesy name was Hailing, came from Hefei in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪陷安慶，皖北土匪紛起，盛波兄弟六人，團練鄉勇​​保衛鄉里，屢出殺賊。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels took Anqing; bandits rose everywhere in north Anhui; Shengbo and five brothers trained local braves to defend their township and went out repeatedly to kill rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, when the Taiping rebels seized Anqing and banditry erupted across northern Anhui, Shengbo and his five brothers organized local militia to defend their home district and repeatedly sallied forth against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 兄盛華及弟三人皆死事，惟存盛波與弟盛傳，以勇名。

translations.literal: His elder brother Shenghua and three younger brothers all died in service; only Shengbo and his younger brother Shengchuan remained, famed for valor.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Shenghua and three younger brothers all died in action; only Shengbo and his brother Shengchuan survived, both renowned for courage.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成、陳得才等屢擾境，盛波等以練丁二千隨方迎敵，相持數年，遂越境出剿近縣，餉械皆所自備，累獎守備。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng, Chen Decai, and others repeatedly harassed the borders; Shengbo and the others with two thousand trained men met the enemy wherever they came, held out for several years, then crossed the border to suppress rebels in nearby counties; pay and arms were all self-provided; he was repeatedly rewarded as garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng, Chen Decai, and others raided the district repeatedly. Shengbo and his men, two thousand militia strong, met every threat as it came and held their ground for years before crossing into neighboring counties on punitive expeditions, supplying their own pay and arms. He was repeatedly commended and promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章募淮軍援江蘇，令盛波就所部選募成軍，曰盛字營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Li Hongzhang raised the Huai Army to relieve Jiangsu and ordered Shengbo to select and recruit from his command into a full army, called the Shengzi Battalion.
