translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Li Hongzhang raised the Huai Army for Jiangsu, Shengbo was ordered to select and recruit from his followers into a formal regiment, the Shengzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 從至上海，破賊於北新涇，擢游擊。

translations.literal: Following to Shanghai, he defeated rebels at Beixinjing and was promoted to acting major.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the army to Shanghai, routed the rebels at Beixinjing, and was promoted to brevet major.

sentences.zh: 又大破賊於四江口，賜號卓勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: He again routed rebels utterly at Sikou and was granted the title Zhuoyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: He won another crushing victory at Sikou and was granted the title Zhuoyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 二年，克太倉，進崑山，扼雙鳳橋，复縣城。

translations.literal: In the second year he took Taicang, advanced on Kunshan, held Shuangfeng Bridge, and recovered the county seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he captured Taicang, advanced on Kunshan, seized Shuangfeng Bridge, and recovered the county seat.

sentences.zh: 破麥市橋賊壘，擢副將。

translations.literal: He broke the rebel fort at Maishi Bridge and was promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the rebel stockade at Maishi Bridge and was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 進攻江陰，擊敗援賊。

translations.literal: Advancing against Jiangyin, he defeated relief rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Jiangyin he routed the relief columns.

sentences.zh: 會克縣城，以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Joining in he took the county seat and was entered as major general.
translations.idiomatic: He joined in the capture of the county seat and was nominated major general.

sentences.zh: 會攻無錫，毀賊船百餘，破惠山石卡，擒賊酋黃子隆，以提督記名，予一品封典。

translations.literal: Joining the attack on Wuxi, he destroyed more than a hundred rebel boats, broke the stone barrier at Huishan, captured the rebel chief Huang Zilong, was entered as provincial commander-in-chief, and granted a first-rank patent of nobility.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Wuxi he destroyed more than a hundred rebel vessels, stormed the stone barrier at Huishan, and captured the rebel leader Huang Zilong. He was nominated provincial military governor and granted a first-rank patent of nobility.

sentences.zh: 三年，合圍常州，盛波由小南門攻入。

translations.literal: In the third year the encirclement of Changzhou closed; Shengbo entered through the Lesser South Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when the siege of Changzhou closed, Shengbo led the assault through the Lesser South Gate.

sentences.zh: 賊首就擒，以總兵侭先題奏。

translations.literal: The rebel chiefs were captured; as major general he was among the first to memorialize the victory.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leaders were taken prisoner, and as major general he was among the first to report the victory to the throne.

sentences.zh: 時江寧已復，餘黨黃文英走踞廣德，盛波追之至橫山，文英遁走。

translations.literal: Nanjing had already been recovered; remnant faction Huang Wenying fled to hold Guangde; Shengbo pursued to Hengshan and Wenying slipped away.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing had already fallen to the Qing, but the remnant leader Huang Wenying seized Guangde. Shengbo pursued him to Hengshan, where Wenying escaped.

sentences.zh: 城賊拒戰，敗之，复廣德，進至寧國境而還，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: The city rebels resisted battle and were defeated; Guangde was recovered; he advanced to the border of Ningguo and returned; the yellow riding jacket was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels in the city resisted and were defeated; Guangde was recovered; he advanced to the border of Ningguo and withdrew, and was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 四年，從曾國籓剿捻匪。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed Zeng Guofan in suppressing Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined Zeng Guofan in the campaign against the Nian rebels.

sentences.zh: 張總愚圍雉河集，盛波赴援，循渦河岸破賊。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyu besieged Zhiheji; Shengbo went to relieve it and along the Guo River bank defeated rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Zongyu besieged Zhiheji, Shengbo marched to relieve the town and routed the rebels along the Guo River.

sentences.zh: 英翰軍突圍夾擊，圍始解。

translations.literal: Yinghan's army broke out and attacked from both sides; the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Yinghan's force broke out of the encirclement in a pincer attack, and the siege was finally raised.

sentences.zh: 授甘肅涼州鎮總兵，敗捻匪於寧陵。

translations.literal: He was appointed commander of the Liangzhou Garrison in Gansu and defeated Nian bandits at Ningling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander of the Liangzhou Garrison in Gansu and defeated Nian rebels at Ningling.

sentences.zh: 五年，拔菏澤遊莊寨、方埠賊巢，被珍賚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he took the rebel nests at Youzhuang Stockade and Fangbu in Heze and received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he stormed the rebel strongholds at Youzhuang and Fangbu near Heze and received imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 牛洛紅竄亳州，截擊於白龍王廟，大破之。

translations.literal: Niu Luohong fled into Bozhou; he intercepted at Bailongwang Temple and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When Niu Luohong broke into Bozhou, Shengbo intercepted him at Bailongwang Temple and inflicted a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，追賊雲夢，連敗之於兩河口、沙河、胡家店。

translations.literal: That winter he pursued rebels to Yunmeng and in succession defeated them at Lianghekou, Shahe, and Hujiadian.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he pursued the rebels into Yunmeng and routed them in succession at Lianghekou, Shahe, and Hujiadian.

sentences.zh: 六年，躡追任柱至信陽，與弟盛傳分路蹙之台子畈山中，賊舍騎四竄，追及談家河，擒賊目汪老魁等。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he pursued Ren Zhu to Xinyang; with his younger brother Shengchuan he divided routes to hem him in the Taizifan mountains; rebels abandoned their horses and fled in four directions; he caught up at Tanjia River and captured rebel officers Wang Laokui and others.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he pursued Ren Zhu to Xinyang and, with his brother Shengchuan, split forces to corner him in the Taizifan hills. The rebels abandoned their horses and scattered in all directions; Shengbo caught up at Tanjia River and captured the rebel officers Wang Laokui and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 賴文光來援，复擊敗之。

translations.literal: Lai Wenguang came in relief and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When Lai Wenguang came to relieve them, Shengbo defeated him as well.

sentences.zh: 九月，破沭陽程寨賊，又敗之於石榴寨、高家寨，追至海州阿胡鎮，殲悍黨趙天福，東捻尋平。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he broke the rebels at Chengzai in Shuyang, again defeated them at Shiliuzhai and Gaojiazhai, pursued to Ahu Town in Haizhou, annihilated the fierce band under Zhao Tianfu, and the Eastern Nian were soon pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he stormed the rebel camp at Chengzai in Shuyang, routed them again at Shiliuzhai and Gaojiazhai, pursued them to Ahu in Haizhou, and wiped out the hardened fighter Zhao Tianfu. The Eastern Nian were soon suppressed.

sentences.zh: 七年，西捻張總愚竄畿輔，盛波追至陵縣土橋，馬步合擊，賊潰走。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the Western Nian leader Zhang Zongyu fled into the capital region; Shengbo pursued to Tuqiao in Ling County; cavalry and infantry attacked together and the rebels routed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Zhang Zongyu and the Western Nian broke into the metropolitan region. Shengbo pursued them to Tuqiao in Ling County, where a combined cavalry and infantry assault sent the rebels fleeing in rout.

sentences.zh: 五月，盛波駐毛家莊，賊由吳橋來犯，設伏痛擊，斬級數千。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Shengbo garrisoned Maojia Village; rebels came from Wuqiao to attack; he set an ambush and struck fiercely, beheading several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, while garrisoned at Maojia Village, he ambushed rebels advancing from Wuqiao and killed several thousand of them.

sentences.zh: 襲賊於楊丁莊，陣斬總愚之侄張三彪。

translations.literal: He raided rebels at Yangding Village and killed Zongyu's nephew Zhang Sanbiao in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He surprised the rebels at Yangding Village and killed Zongyu's nephew Zhang Sanbiao on the field.

sentences.zh: 六月，會擊於茌平，總愚走死。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he joined the attack at Chiping; Zongyu fled and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he joined the assault at Chiping, where Zongyu fled to his death.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，晉號福齡阿巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the Western Nian were pacified, he was advanced to the title Fuling'a Batür.
translations.idiomatic: With the Western Nian suppressed, he was promoted to the title Fuling'a Batür.

sentences.zh: 軍事定，以母老陳請回籍終養，尋以前年所部攻破河南唐縣民寨，慘斃多命，為巡撫李鶴年所劾，褫職，交李鴻章按治，以盛波身在前敵，免其科罪。

translations.literal: When military affairs were settled, citing his aged mother he memorialized to return home for lifelong care; soon afterward, because the year before his troops had stormed a civilian stockade in Tang County, Henan, and many lives were cruelly ended, he was impeached by Governor Li Henian, stripped of office, and handed to Li Hongzhang for investigation; because Shengbo was himself at the front line, he was exempted from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When the fighting ended he asked to return home to care for his aged mother. Soon afterward, however, his troops' assault the previous year on a civilian stockade in Tang County, Henan, in which many innocents were killed, led Governor Li Henian to impeach him and strip him of rank. The case was referred to Li Hongzhang for investigation, but because Shengbo had been at the front in person, he was spared formal punishment.

sentences.zh: 九年，鴻章疏陳盛波功多，復原官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Hongzhang memorialized that Shengbo's merits were many and his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Li Hongzhang memorialized on Shengbo's many services, and his former rank was restored.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，命在淮北選募精壯十營赴天津備防，責司訓練。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu he was ordered to select and recruit ten battalions of elite troops north of the Huai for defense at Tianjin and charged with their training.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Guangxu he was ordered to raise ten battalions of picked men north of the Huai for the Tianjin garrison and placed in charge of their training.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂，奏，許弟盛傳回籍治喪，盛波仍留營。

translations.literal: In mourning for his mother he memorialized; his younger brother Shengchuan was permitted to return home to conduct the funeral while Shengbo remained in camp.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he memorialized the court; his brother Shengchuan was allowed to return home for the funeral while Shengbo stayed with the troops.

sentences.zh: 盛傳尋卒，所遺湖南提督即以盛波代署，疏辭，不允。

translations.literal: Shengchuan soon died; the vacant post of Hunan provincial commander-in-chief left by him was given to Shengbo to act in; he memorialized to decline and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Shengchuan died soon afterward, and Shengbo was appointed acting Hunan provincial military governor in his place. He memorialized to decline but was overruled.

sentences.zh: 服闋，實授。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he received substantive appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, he received the appointment in full.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏陳戰績，謂其治軍嚴而不苛，人樂為用。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized his battle record, saying his governance of troops was strict but not harsh and men were glad to serve under him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized his battle record, praising his command as strict but fair, so that his men served willingly.

sentences.zh: 善察地勢，審賊情，部曲經其指授，輒有家法。

translations.literal: He was skilled at observing terrain and assessing rebel situations; troops under his instruction always had his household methods.
translations.idiomatic: He had a keen eye for terrain and enemy dispositions, and the units he trained fought by methods all their own.

sentences.zh: 防海以來，所部為淮軍最大之軍，諸軍勳望無出其右。

translations.literal: Since coastal defense began, his command was the largest force in the Huai Army, and among all armies none matched his merit and standing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the coastal defense campaigns his command had been the largest formation in the Huai Army, and no other general matched his record or prestige.

sentences.zh: 詔優恤，建專祠，諡剛敏。

translations.literal: An edict granted favorable mourning favors, built a dedicated shrine, and gave the posthumous title Gangmin.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted generous posthumous honors, a dedicated shrine was erected, and he received the posthumous name Gangmin (Steadfast and Keen).

sentences.zh: 周盛傳，字薪如，盛波之弟。

translations.literal: Zhou Shengchuan, styled Xinru, was Shengbo's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Shengchuan, whose courtesy name was Xinru, was the younger brother of Zhou Shengbo.

sentences.zh: 盛傳偕諸兄集丁壯團練。

translations.literal: Shengchuan together with his elder brothers gathered able-bodied men for militia training.
translations.idiomatic: Shengchuan and his elder brothers gathered local militia from among the able-bodied men of the district.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪擾合肥，率百餘人擊敗之，擒賊目馬千祿。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels harassed Hefei; he led more than a hundred men to defeat them and captured the rebel officer Ma Qianlu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng, when Taiping rebels raided Hefei, he led a little over a hundred men to defeat them and captured the rebel officer Ma Qianlu.

sentences.zh: 五年，兄盛華陣亡，盛傳與盛波分領團從，防戰數有功，獎敘把總。

translations.literal: In the fifth year his elder brother Shenghua died in battle; Shengchuan and Shengbo divided command of the militia followers; in defense and battle he had merit several times and was rewarded with registration as platoon leader.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his brother Shenghua was killed in action. Shengchuan and Shengbo split command of the militia, and after several successful defensive engagements he was registered as a platoon leader.

sentences.zh: 十一年，赴援壽州，擢千總。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went to relieve Shouzhou and was promoted to company commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he marched to relieve Shouzhou and was promoted to company commander.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，盛波從李鴻章援江蘇，盛傳充親兵營哨官，從克嘉定及戰四江口，累擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi Shengbo followed Li Hongzhang to relieve Jiangsu; Shengchuan served as platoon officer of the personal guard battalion, followed in taking Jiading and fighting at Sikou, and was repeatedly promoted to acting major.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi, when Shengbo followed Li Hongzhang to Jiangsu, Shengchuan served as an officer in the personal guard battalion, took part in the capture of Jiading and the battle at Sikou, and rose by stages to brevet major.

sentences.zh: 二年，回籍增募勇丁，會攻太倉，賊酋蔡元隆詐降，設伏狙擊官軍，盛傳獨嚴備，不為所挫。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned home to recruit more braves, joined the attack on Taicang; the rebel chief Cai Yuanlong feigned surrender and set an ambush to strike the government army; Shengchuan alone was strictly on guard and was not foiled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he returned home to recruit more troops and joined the assault on Taicang. When the rebel leader Cai Yuanlong pretended to surrender and laid an ambush for the imperial forces, Shengchuan alone kept his men on strict alert and was not caught off guard.

sentences.zh: 越數日，偕諸軍一鼓克之，駐軍雙鳳鎮，為賊所圍，連戰三晝夜，破之，克崑山，賜號勳勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Several days later, together with the armies he took it in one assault; he garrisoned Shuangfeng Town, was surrounded by rebels, fought three days and nights in succession, broke them, took Kunshan, and was granted the title Xunyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: Days later he joined the allied columns in a single assault that took the city. He garrisoned Shuangfeng Town, was besieged by rebels, and fought for three days and nights before breaking the encirclement and capturing Kunshan. He was granted the title Xunyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 攻江陰，毀東門賊營，城复，擢參將。

translations.literal: Attacking Jiangyin, he destroyed the rebel camp at the east gate; the city was recovered and he was promoted to lieutenant colonel.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Jiangyin he destroyed the rebel camp at the east gate; when the city fell he was promoted to colonel.

sentences.zh: 迭戰東亭鎮、興隆橋、鴨城橋、西倉，遂克無錫，功尤多，超擢以總兵記名。

translations.literal: Fighting in succession at Dongting Town, Xinglong Bridge, Yacheng Bridge, and Xicang, he then took Wuxi; his merit was especially great and he was exceptionally promoted to nomination as major general.
translations.idiomatic: He fought in succession at Dongting, Xinglong Bridge, Yacheng Bridge, and Xicang, then captured Wuxi. His contributions ranked especially high, and he was exceptionally nominated major general.

sentences.zh: 進攻常州，三年，進逼郡城南門，賊突出拒，盛傳且戰且築營，賊屢抄後路，皆擊退。

translations.literal: Advancing against Changzhou, in the third year he pressed close to the south gate of the prefectural city; rebels sallied to resist; Shengchuan fought while building camps; rebels repeatedly outflanked his rear and were all repulsed.
translations.idiomatic: In the assault on Changzhou, in the third year he closed on the city's south gate. When rebels sallied out to resist, Shengchuan fought while throwing up camps, beating back every attempt to turn his rear.

sentences.zh: 登石橋督戰，橋斷墮水，又受砲傷，絕而復甦。

translations.literal: He mounted a stone bridge to direct battle; the bridge broke and he fell into the water; he also took a cannon wound, lost consciousness and revived.
translations.idiomatic: He climbed a stone bridge to direct the fighting; the bridge gave way and he plunged into the water. Struck by a cannonball, he lost consciousness but came to again.

sentences.zh: 越數日，裹創會攻，攀城先登。

translations.literal: Several days later, binding his wounds he joined the assault and was first to scale the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Days later, his wounds bound, he joined the assault and was the first man up the wall.

sentences.zh: 克常州，詔以總兵遇缺先行題奏，加提督銜。

translations.literal: When Changzhou was taken, an edict ordered that when a major general vacancy arose he be memorialized first; he was given the brevet rank of provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhou fell, an edict directed that he be the first nominated when a major general vacancy opened, and he was granted the honorary title of provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 以撫標親兵三營改為傳字營，盛傳始獨領一軍，移防溧陽。

translations.literal: Three battalions of the governor's personal guard were converted into the Chuanzi Battalion; Shengchuan for the first time commanded an army alone and was transferred to garrison Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Three battalions of the governor's personal guard were reorganized as the Chuanzi Battalion, and Shengchuan commanded an independent force for the first time, transferred to garrison Liyang.

sentences.zh: 尋會銘軍克廣德州。

translations.literal: Before long he joined Mingchuan's army in taking Guangde Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Liu Mingchuan's force in capturing Guangde.

sentences.zh: 四年，調剿捻匪，偕兄盛波援雉河集，自睢寧、宿州轉戰而前。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to suppress Nian bandits; together with his elder brother Shengbo he relieved Zhiheji, fighting forward from Suining and Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was assigned to operations against the Nian, marching with his brother Shengbo to relieve Zhiheji and fighting his way forward from Suining and Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 將至，捻酋任柱以馬隊突犯，盛傳堅陣不動，出奇兵抄賊後，賊始卻，會諸軍夾擊，賊潰​​走，以提督記名。

translations.literal: As he was about to arrive, the Nian chief Ren Zhu charged with his cavalry; Shengchuan held formation unmoved, sent exceptional troops to outflank the rebels' rear; the rebels then retreated; joining the armies in attack from both sides the rebels routed and fled; he was entered as provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: As he approached, the Nian leader Ren Zhu charged with his cavalry. Shengchuan held his line firm, sent a flanking force around the enemy rear, and only then did the rebels pull back. A pincer attack with allied troops sent them fleeing in rout, and he was nominated provincial military governor.

sentences.zh: 移防歸德。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Guide.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison Guide.

sentences.zh: 五年春，迭敗賊於考城、鉅野、城武、菏澤，詔嘉盛傳兄弟苦戰，同被珍賚。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fifth year he in succession defeated rebels at Kaocheng, Juye, Chengwu, and Heze; an edict praised the Shengchuan brothers' bitter fighting and both received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he routed the rebels in succession at Kaocheng, Juye, Chengwu, and Heze. An edict commended the brothers' grueling campaigns, and both received imperial rewards.

sentences.zh: 五月，偕盛波破牛洛紅於亳州，​​洛紅被創夜遁，道死。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, together with Shengbo he defeated Niu Luohong at Bozhou; Luohong was wounded and fled by night and died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he and Shengbo defeated Niu Luohong at Bozhou; Luohong was wounded, fled by night, and died on the road.

sentences.zh: 追賊扶溝、鄢陵、許州，扼防周家口。

translations.literal: He pursued rebels through Fugou, Yanling, and Xuzhou and held defense at Zhoujiakou.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels through Fugou, Yanling, and Xuzhou and sealed the line at Zhoujiakou.

sentences.zh: 時以長圍困賊，盛傳築賈魯河長牆，檄調為游擊之師，解柘城、羅山圍。

translations.literal: At the time a long encirclement was used to trap rebels; Shengchuan built a long wall along the Jialu River, was ordered by dispatch to become a mobile striking force, and lifted the sieges of Zhecheng and Luoshan.
translations.idiomatic: While a long encirclement strategy was in force, Shengchuan built a wall along the Jialu River, was reassigned as a mobile strike column, and raised the sieges of Zhecheng and Luoshan.

sentences.zh: 六年，授廣西右江鎮總兵，偕盛波蹙賊信陽譚家河，斬馘逾萬。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was appointed commander of the Youjiang Garrison in Guangxi; together with Shengbo he hemmed in rebels at Tanjia River in Xinyang and beheaded more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed commander of the Youjiang Garrison in Guangxi. With Shengbo he cornered the rebels at Tanjia River near Xinyang and killed more than ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 追賊入山東，至江北海州，捻匪大衰。

translations.literal: Pursuing rebels into Shandong, to Haizhou north of the Yangzi, the Nian bandits greatly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued the rebels into Shandong as far as Haizhou on the north Jiangsu coast, and the Nian movement went into steep decline.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，任柱、賴文光均就殲。

translations.literal: That winter Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang were both annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: That winter both Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 七年春，偕盛波渡河會剿張總愚，敗賊於山東、直隸之間，守運河長牆。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, together with Shengbo he crossed the river to join in suppressing Zhang Zongyu, defeated rebels between Shandong and Zhili, and guarded the long wall along the Grand Canal.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he crossed the river with Shengbo to join operations against Zhang Zongyu, defeated rebels in the Shandong–Zhili borderlands, and held the long embankment along the Grand Canal.

sentences.zh: 盛傳伏炸砲於吳橋毛家莊，合馬步逼賊入伏，砲發，賊屍蔽野。

translations.literal: Shengchuan laid explosive cannon at Maojia Village in Wuqiao; combining cavalry and infantry he forced rebels into the ambush; the cannon fired and rebel corpses covered the field.
translations.idiomatic: Shengchuan set explosive charges at Maojia Village near Wuqiao, drove the rebels into the trap with combined cavalry and infantry, and detonated the mines until rebel dead covered the field.

sentences.zh: 既而茌平合圍，總愚走死，賜黃馬褂。

translations.literal: Before long the encirclement closed at Chiping; Zongyu fled and died; the yellow riding jacket was bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the ring closed at Chiping; Zongyu fled to his death, and Shengchuan was awarded the yellow riding jacket.

sentences.zh: 盛波乞假養親，盛傳代統全軍，從李鴻章移師湖北。

translations.literal: Shengbo begged leave to care for his parents; Shengchuan took command of the whole army in his place and followed Li Hongzhang in moving troops to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengbo took leave to care for his parents, Shengchuan assumed command of the entire force and followed Li Hongzhang's transfer of operations to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 九年，從鴻章赴陝西剿回匪，賊踞宜川山中，督軍進剿，破之於河兒川、孔岩寨，分兵於宜、洛、鄜、延之間，以遠勢兜圍，先後擒賊酋馬志龍、戴得勝，北山悉平。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he followed Hongzhang to Shaanxi to suppress Hui bandits; rebels held the mountains of Yichuan; he directed the army in advance, broke them at He'erchuan and Kongyan Stockade, divided forces among Yichuan, Luochuan, Fuzhou, and Yan'an, used distant positions to encircle, in succession captured rebel chiefs Ma Zhilong and Dai Desheng, and the northern hills were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he followed Li Hongzhang to Shaanxi against Hui rebels who held the Yichuan hills. He directed the advance, routed them at He'erchuan and Kongyan Stockade, and deployed columns across Yichuan, Luochuan, Fuzhou, and Yan'an in a wide encirclement. He captured the rebel leaders Ma Zhilong and Dai Desheng in turn, and the northern hills were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，鴻章移督直隸，疏調盛傳率所部屯衛畿輔。

translations.literal: That autumn Hongzhang was transferred to govern Zhili; he memorialized to transfer Shengchuan to lead his command in garrisoning the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, when Li Hongzhang was transferred to govern Zhili, he memorialized to bring Shengchuan and his troops to garrison the metropolitan region.

sentences.zh: 十年，移屯青縣馬廠。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he moved his encampment to Machang in Qing County.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he shifted his headquarters to Machang in Qing County.

sentences.zh: 十二年，興脩大沽北塘砲台，築內外土城各一，大砲台三，環置小砲七十有一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he undertook construction of the Beitang batteries at Dagu, built one inner and one outer earthen wall each, three large batteries, and set seventy-one small guns around them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he oversaw construction of the Beitang fortifications at Dagu: inner and outer earthen ramparts, three main batteries, and seventy-one smaller guns emplaced around them.

sentences.zh: 兵房、藥庫、倉廒、義塾及城外溝、河、橋、徬悉備，以所部任其役，捐盛軍欠餉以濟工費。

translations.literal: Barracks, powder magazines, granaries, charity schools, and outside the walls ditches, rivers, bridges, and lodges were all provided; his command performed the labor; he donated the Sheng Army's arrears in pay to cover construction costs.
translations.idiomatic: Barracks, powder magazines, storehouses, charity schools, and the ditches, canals, bridges, and lodges outside the walls were all completed. His troops supplied the labor, and he donated unpaid back pay owed to the Sheng Army to cover construction costs.

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，工竣，詔遇提督缺出先行簡放。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year the work was completed; an edict ordered that when a provincial commander-in-chief vacancy arose he be appointed first.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the thirteenth year the works were finished, and an edict directed that he be the first appointed when a provincial military governor vacancy opened.

sentences.zh: 時鴻章奉敕興復京畿水利，盛傳任津沽屯田事，履勘天津東南縱橫百餘裡，沮洳蕪廢，議疏潦、濬河渠，引淡滌咸，以變斥鹵。

translations.literal: At the time Hongzhang received orders to restore water conservancy in the capital region; Shengchuan was charged with Tianjin garrison colony affairs; he surveyed on foot more than a hundred li east and south of Tianjin, marshy and waste land; he proposed draining floods, dredging canals, leading fresh water to wash away salt, to transform saline soil.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang had been ordered to restore waterworks in the capital region, and Shengchuan was put in charge of the Tianjin garrison colonies. He surveyed on foot more than a hundred li southeast of Tianjin—waterlogged, abandoned land—and proposed flood drainage, canal dredging, and bringing fresh water to flush out salinity and reclaim the barren flats.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，調天津鎮，移屯興工，開南運減河，自靳官屯抵大沽海口，減河兩岸各開支河一、橫河六，溝澮河渠悉如法。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was transferred to the Tianjin Garrison, moved his camp to Xinggong to start work, opened the southern Grand Canal relief channel from Jinguantun to the Dagu estuary, opened one branch river and six cross-rivers on each bank of the relief channel, and ditches and canals all according to method.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he was appointed to the Tianjin Garrison and moved his base to Xinggong to begin works. He opened the southern Grand Canal relief channel from Jinguantun to the Dagu estuary, with one branch canal and six transverse canals on each bank, and subsidiary ditches laid out to standard.

sentences.zh: 建橋徬五十餘處，備蓄洩，使淡水鹹水不相滲混，成稻田六萬餘畝。

translations.literal: He built more than fifty bridges and lodges, prepared storage and drainage, kept fresh and salt water from seeping together, and formed more than sixty thousand mu of rice fields.
translations.idiomatic: He built more than fifty bridges and sluice stations, regulated storage and drainage so fresh and salt water did not mix, and brought more than sixty thousand mu under rice cultivation.

sentences.zh: 濱河斥鹵地沾水利，可墾以億計。

translations.literal: Saline land along the river touched by the water works could be reclaimed on a scale reckoned in hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: The saline flats along the river, once touched by the new water system, could be reclaimed on a scale beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 至六年工竣。

translations.literal: By the sixth year the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The project was completed in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢湖南提督，仍留鎮訓練士卒，悉用西法，著操槍章程十二篇，軍中以為法式。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted to Hunan provincial commander-in-chief, still remaining at his garrison to train soldiers, all using Western methods; he composed twelve chapters of regulations for musket drill, and the army took them as standard method.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Hunan provincial military governor while remaining at his post to train troops entirely by Western methods. He wrote twelve chapters of musket drill regulations that became the army's standard.

sentences.zh: 十年，丁母憂，命改署理，予假回籍治喪。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, in mourning for his mother, he was ordered to change to acting appointment and granted leave to return home to conduct the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when his mother died, he was placed on acting status and granted leave to return home for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 盛傳事親孝，未幾，以哀毀傷發卒，詔優恤，諡武壯，建專祠。

translations.literal: Shengchuan was filial in serving his parents; before long, from grief and mourning wounds broke out and he died; an edict granted favorable mourning favors; posthumous title Wuzhuang; a dedicated shrine was built.
translations.idiomatic: Shengchuan had been devoted to his parents. He died soon afterward when grief brought on a relapse of old wounds. The court granted generous posthumous honors, gave him the name Wuzhuang (Martial and Stalwart), and erected a dedicated shrine.

sentences.zh: 潘鼎新，字琴軒，安徽廬江人。

translations.literal: Pan Dingxin, styled Qinxuan, was a native of Lujiang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dingxin, whose courtesy name was Qinxuan, came from Lujiang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年舉人，議敘知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination; by deliberation he was registered as magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial civil examination in the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang and was registered for appointment as a county magistrate.

sentences.zh: 咸豐七年，投★安徽軍營，從克霍山，擢同知。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Xianfeng he entered the Anhui army camp, followed in taking Huoshan, and was promoted to sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Xianfeng he entered service in the Anhui army, took part in the capture of Huoshan, and was promoted to sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 十一年，父璞領鄉團助剿，被執不屈死。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year his father Pu led local militia to assist in suppression, was captured, refused to submit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year his father Pu led local militia in support of government operations, was captured, refused to yield, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 鼎新誓殺賊復仇，請分兵攻三河鎮，克之，負父骸歸。

translations.literal: Dingxin swore to kill rebels and avenge his father, requested divided forces to attack Sanhe Town, took it, and carried his father's remains home.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxin swore to kill the rebels and avenge his father, secured a detachment to attack Sanhe, captured the town, and brought his father's body home.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓聞而壯之，時方創淮軍，令募勇立鼎字營。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan heard and admired this; at the time the Huai Army was just being created; he ordered recruitment of braves to establish the Dingzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan was impressed when he heard of it. As the Huai Army was being formed, he ordered Dingxin to raise troops and establish the Dingzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從李鴻章援上海，連克奉賢、川沙、南匯，以知府用。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to relieve Shanghai, in succession took Fengxian, Chuansha, and Nanhui, and was employed as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, captured Fengxian, Chuansha, and Nanhui in succession, and was appointed acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 克金山，又破賊虹橋，擢道員。

translations.literal: He took Jinshan and again defeated rebels at Hongqiao; he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Jinshan and routed the rebels at Hongqiao, earning promotion to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 二年，攻福山鎮，鼎新以開花砲炸賊壘，克之，解常熟圍，授江蘇常鎮通海道，以父喪未除，改署任。

translations.literal: In the second year he attacked Fushan Town; Dingxin used explosive shells to blast rebel forts and took it, lifting the siege of Changshu; he was appointed Jiangsu Chang-Zhen-Tonghai Circuit; as his father's mourning was not yet completed, it was changed to acting appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he assaulted Fushan. Dingxin used explosive shells to demolish the rebel stockades, took the town, and raised the siege of Changshu. He was appointed to the Chang-Zhen-Tonghai circuit in Jiangsu, but because he was still in mourning for his father the post was made acting.

sentences.zh: 連破賊於楓涇及嘉善、西塘，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: In succession he defeated rebels at Fengjing and at Jiashan and Xitang; he was given the brevet rank of provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He routed the rebels in succession at Fengjing, Jiashan, and Xitang, and was granted the honorary title of provincial surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 克平湖、乍浦、海鹽，獲賊銀三十餘萬兩充餉。

translations.literal: He took Pinghu, Zhapu, and Haiyan, seized more than three hundred thousand taels of rebel silver to supply pay.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Pinghu, Zhapu, and Haiyan and seized more than three hundred thousand taels of rebel silver for army pay.

sentences.zh: 破賊於興城、沈盪、新豐。

translations.literal: He defeated rebels at Xingcheng, Shendang, and Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the rebels at Xingcheng, Shendang, and Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 三年，會克嘉興，戰吳漊、南潯，會攻湖州，賊拒守晟舍，攻兩晝夜，傷脅，破升山九壘，奪三里橋，直抵城下，克湖州，加布政使銜，賜號敢勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the third year he joined in taking Jiaxing, fought at Wulian and Nanxun, joined the attack on Huzhou; rebels defended Shengshe; he attacked two days and nights, was wounded in the flank, broke nine forts on Sheng Hill, seized Sanli Bridge, pressed straight to below the walls, took Huzhou, was given the brevet rank of provincial administration commissioner, and granted the title Ganyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined in the capture of Jiaxing and fought at Wulian and Nanxun. In the assault on Huzhou the rebels held Shengshe; after two days and nights of fighting he took a wound in the side, stormed nine stockades on Sheng Hill, seized Sanli Bridge, and pressed to the city walls. Huzhou fell; he was granted the honorary title of provincial administration commissioner and the name Ganyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 蘇、浙既定，賜黃馬褂，駐屯松江。

translations.literal: When Jiangsu and Zhejiang were settled, the yellow riding jacket was bestowed and he garrisoned Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: With Jiangsu and Zhejiang pacified, he was awarded the yellow riding jacket and garrisoned Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧格林沁戰歿，捻匪益熾，畿輔震動，詔徵勁旅入衛，李鴻章遣鼎新率砲隊航海赴天津。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Sengge Rinchen died in battle; Nian bandits burned ever hotter; the capital region was shaken; an edict summoned crack troops for defense; Li Hongzhang sent Dingxin to lead the artillery column by sea to Tianjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, after Sengge Rinchen fell in battle and the Nian threat surged, the metropolitan region was thrown into alarm. The court summoned elite forces for its defense, and Li Hongzhang sent Dingxin with the artillery column by sea to Tianjin.

sentences.zh: 尋命所部十一營移駐濟寧，擢山東按察使。

translations.literal: Before long his eleven battalions were ordered to move garrison to Jining; he was promoted to Shandong provincial surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his eleven battalions were ordered to Jining, and he was promoted to provincial surveillance commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 擊敗捻首賴文光於豐縣陳家莊，又追敗之於沛縣、魚台、定陶。

translations.literal: He defeated the Nian chief Lai Wenguang at Chenjia Village in Feng County and again pursued and defeated him at Peixian, Yutai, and Dingtao.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Nian leader Lai Wenguang at Chenjiazhuang in Feng County and pursued him to further defeats at Peixian, Yutai, and Dingtao.

sentences.zh: 五年，敗賊於鉅野，解鄆城圍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he defeated rebels at Juye and lifted the siege of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he routed the rebels at Juye and raised the siege of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 築運河沿岸長牆，開黑風口淤河，引泗水灌之。

translations.literal: He built a long wall along the Grand Canal, opened the silted Hei Fengkou river, and led Si River water to irrigate it.
translations.idiomatic: He constructed a long embankment along the Grand Canal, dredged the silted channel at Heifengkou, and diverted the Si River to fill it.

sentences.zh: 賊屢敗於西華、太康，竄至油坊岡，鼎新夾擊，殪其酋。

translations.literal: Rebels were repeatedly defeated at Xihua and Taikang, fled to Youfang Gang; Dingxin attacked from both sides and killed their chief.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated defeats at Xihua and Taikang the rebels fled to Youfang Gang, where Dingxin caught them in a pincer and killed their leader.

sentences.zh: 又追賊鄆城、菏澤、曹縣、東明，竄入河南境，追擊於杞縣柿園、嘉祥臥龍山。

translations.literal: He again pursued rebels through Yancheng, Heze, Caoxian, and Dongming; they fled into Henan territory; he pursued to Shiyuan in Qixian and Wolong Hill in Jiaxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued them through Yancheng, Heze, Caoxian, and Dongming into Henan, catching up with them at Shiyuan in Qixian and Wolong Hill in Jiaxiang.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷山東布政使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Shandong provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 築新河、濰河長牆，會諸軍守之。

translations.literal: He built long walls along the Xin River and Wei River and joined the armies in guarding them.
translations.idiomatic: He built long embankments along the Xin and Wei rivers and coordinated with allied forces to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 賊由東軍汛地偷渡濰河，衝出南竄，都司董金勝率馬隊尾追，敗之莒州、沭陽。

translations.literal: Rebels secretly crossed the Wei River from the eastern army's garrison sector, burst out and fled south; Battalion Commander Dong Jinsheng led cavalry in pursuit and defeated them at Juzhou and Shuyang.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels slipped across the Wei River from the eastern army's sector and broke south. Battalion Commander Dong Jinsheng led the cavalry in pursuit and routed them at Juzhou and Shuyang.

sentences.zh: 鼎新追至海州石榴橋，據山下擊，時賊尚五六萬，連戰於馬陵山、臥龍寨，賊​​張兩翼來犯，鼎新為圓陣，賊不能撼，伺懈突擊，斬馘甚眾。

translations.literal: Dingxin pursued to Shiliuqiao in Haizhou, attacked from the foothills; at the time rebels still numbered fifty or sixty thousand; he fought in succession at Maling Hill and Wolong Stockade; rebels spread both wings to attack; Dingxin formed a circular array; rebels could not shake it; watching for slackness he struck suddenly and beheaded a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxin pursued them to Shiliuqiao near Haizhou and attacked from the hills. The rebels still numbered fifty or sixty thousand. After battles at Maling Hill and Wolong Stockade, they advanced on both wings; Dingxin formed a circular defense they could not break, then struck when they slackened and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 追敗之剡城柴戶店、海州上莊，斬級千餘，殪賊目楊天燕、陳天福，其酋李宗世等乞降，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: Pursuing, he defeated them at Chaihudian in Yancheng and Shangzhuang in Haizhou, beheaded more than a thousand, killed rebel officers Yang Tianyan and Chen Tianfu; their chiefs Li Zongshi and others begged to surrender; he was given the first-rank official's hat ornament.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued and defeated them at Chaihudian and Shangzhuang, taking more than a thousand heads and killing the rebel officers Yang Tianyan and Chen Tianfu. Their leaders Li Zongshi and others surrendered, and Dingxin was awarded the first-rank hat knob.

sentences.zh: 捻首任柱、賴文光先後就殲擒。

translations.literal: The Nian chiefs Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang were in succession annihilated and captured.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian leaders Ren Zhu and Lai Wenguang were killed or captured in turn.

sentences.zh: 七年，馳援畿輔，鼎新至饒陽，賊趨保定，繞其前迎擊，敗之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he rushed to relieve the capital region; Dingxin reached Raoyang; rebels moved toward Baoding; he circled ahead to meet and attack and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he raced to the metropolitan region. At Raoyang, when rebels marched on Baoding, he swung ahead to intercept and routed them.

sentences.zh: 尋破賊於滄州郭橋、柳橋，殪其酋羅六。

translations.literal: Before long he defeated rebels at Guoqiao and Liuqiao in Cangzhou and killed their chief Luo Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He soon defeated the rebels at Guoqiao and Liuqiao in Cangzhou and killed their leader Luo Liu.

sentences.zh: 又戰高唐、吳橋，於捷地開減河，築長牆，抵東昌。

translations.literal: He again fought at Gaotang and Wuqiao, opened a relief channel at Jiedi, built a long wall, and reached Dongchang.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again at Gaotang and Wuqiao, opened a relief canal at Jiedi, built a long embankment, and extended the line to Dongchang.

sentences.zh: 迭蹙賊於德平、陽信、商河，與諸軍合擊。

translations.literal: In succession he pressed rebels at Dezhou, Yangxin, and Shanghe, joining the armies in concerted attack.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the rebels in succession at Dezhou, Yangxin, and Shanghe, coordinating with allied forces in combined attacks.

sentences.zh: 西捻平，予雲騎尉世職，晉一等輕車都尉。

translations.literal: When the Western Nian were pacified, he was granted the hereditary post of Cloud Cavalry Commandant and advanced to first-rank Commandant of Light Chariots.
translations.idiomatic: With the Western Nian suppressed, he received the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant and was promoted to first-rank Commandant of Light Chariots.

sentences.zh: 尋命從左宗棠剿回匪，鼎新請開缺省親。

translations.literal: Before long he was ordered to follow Zuo Zongtang in suppressing Hui bandits; Dingxin requested leave of office to visit his family.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to join Zuo Zongtang against the Hui rebels, but Dingxin asked to resign his post and return home.

sentences.zh: 九年，丁母憂。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was in mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 服闋，李鴻章奏留辦天津海防。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, Li Hongzhang memorialized to retain him to manage Tianjin coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, Li Hongzhang memorialized to keep him in charge of Tianjin's coastal defenses.

sentences.zh: 十三年，授雲南布政使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was appointed Yunnan provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was appointed provincial administration commissioner of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 光緒二年，就擢巡撫，與總督劉長佑不合，三年，命來京另候簡用，乞假歸。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangxu he was promoted in place to governor; he did not get along with Governor-General Liu Changyou; in the third year he was ordered to come to the capital to await another appointment and begged leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangxu he was promoted to governor of Yunnan but clashed with Governor-General Liu Changyou. In the third year he was recalled to Beijing to await reassignment and asked leave to return home.

sentences.zh: 五年，召天津隨辦防務，七年，回籍。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was summoned to Tianjin to assist in defense affairs; in the seventh year he returned to his native place.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was called to Tianjin to assist in defense work; in the seventh year he went home.

sentences.zh: 十年，法越兵事起，起署湖南巡撫，調授廣西巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Franco-Vietnamese war arose; he was recalled to act as Governor of Hunan and transferred to appoint as Governor of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when war broke out between France and Vietnam, he was recalled to serve as acting governor of Hunan and then appointed governor of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 時徐延旭出關兵挫，故以鼎新代之，命按治提督黃桂蘭等失律罪，讞擬輕縱，嚴旨斥責。

translations.literal: At the time Xu Yanxu had suffered defeat after crossing the border, so Dingxin replaced him; he was ordered to investigate the crimes of Provincial Commander Huang Guilan and others for breach of discipline; his verdict proposed leniency and was sternly rebuked by imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanxu had been defeated after leading troops across the border, so Dingxin replaced him. Ordered to try Provincial Commander Huang Guilan and others for disciplinary failures, he proposed overly lenient sentences and received a stern imperial rebuke.

sentences.zh: 命督軍進諒山，扼屯梅谷、松堅牢諸隘，鼎新奏請諸軍歸雲貴總督岑毓英節制，自為之副，不允。

translations.literal: He was ordered to direct the army in advancing on Lang Son and hold the passes at Meigu, Songjianlao, and others; Dingxin memorialized that all armies be placed under the command of Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Cen Yuying with himself as deputy; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to advance on Lang Son and hold passes including Meigu and Songjianlao, Dingxin asked that all forces be placed under Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General Cen Yuying with himself as deputy. The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 又私謂終歸和局，以節餉為主，不得士心。

translations.literal: He also said privately that matters would end in peace talks and that saving pay was the main concern, and he did not win the hearts of the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He also let it be known privately that the war would end in negotiation and that cutting costs mattered most, and he never won the soldiers' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 初戰船頭、紙作社，奏捷。

translations.literal: In initial battles at Chuantou and Zhizuoshe he reported victory.
translations.idiomatic: Early engagements at Chuantou and Zhizuoshe were reported as victories.

sentences.zh: 十二月，法兵大舉來犯，諒山陷，師退，自請治罪，詔帶罪立功。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month French troops came in force; Lang Son fell; the army retreated; he asked to be punished; an edict ordered him to perform merit while bearing guilt.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the French launched a major offensive; Lang Son fell and the army retreated. Dingxin asked to be punished, but an edict ordered him to redeem himself through further service.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月，鎮南關失守，總兵楊玉科戰死，喪提督劉恩河以次十餘員。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year Zhennan Pass was lost; Major General Yang Yuke died in battle; more than ten officers were lost including Provincial Commander Liu Enhe and those below.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year Zhennan Pass fell. Major General Yang Yuke was killed in battle, and more than a dozen officers including Provincial Commander Liu Enhe were lost.

sentences.zh: 鼎新傷肘墜馬，倉皇失措，退至龍州，詔奪職。

translations.literal: Dingxin was wounded in the elbow and fell from his horse; in panic and disorder he retreated to Longzhou; an edict stripped him of office.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxin took a wound to the elbow and fell from his horse. In disarray he retreated to Longzhou, and an edict stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 法兵由艽封窺龍州，賴馮子材、蘇元春、王德榜諸軍力戰，大破之，复鎮南關，追躡連捷，克諒山。

translations.literal: French troops peered toward Longzhou from Qiefeng; relying on Feng Zicai, Su Yuanchun, Wang Debang, and other armies fighting fiercely, they were utterly routed; Zhennan Pass was recovered; pursuit brought successive victories and Lang Son was taken.
translations.idiomatic: When French troops threatened Longzhou from Qiefeng, Feng Zicai, Su Yuanchun, Wang Debang, and other commanders fought them off decisively, recovered Zhennan Pass, pursued with repeated victories, and retook Lang Son.

sentences.zh: 和議旋成，鼎新乃解任回籍。

translations.literal: Peace was soon concluded; Dingxin then resigned his post and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Peace was soon concluded, and Dingxin resigned and returned home.

sentences.zh: 十四年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home in the fourteenth year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章疏陳前功，乞恩復原官。

translations.literal: Li Hongzhang memorialized his former merits and begged favor to restore his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang memorialized his earlier services and asked that his former rank be posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 吳長慶，字筱軒，安徽廬江人。

translations.literal: Wu Changqing, styled Xiaoxuan, was a native of Lujiang in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changqing, whose courtesy name was Xiaoxuan, came from Lujiang in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 父廷香，在籍治團練，咸豐四年，殉寇難，卹，予雲騎尉世職，見忠義傳。

translations.literal: His father Tingxiang managed local militia training at home; in the fourth year of Xianfeng he died for the realm resisting bandits; mourning favors were granted and the hereditary post of Cloud Cavalry Commandant given; see the Loyalty and Righteousness biography.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingxiang had organized local militia at home and died resisting invaders in the fourth year of Xianfeng. Posthumous honors were granted, including the hereditary rank of Cloud Cavalry Commandant; he is treated in the biographies of the loyal and righteous.

sentences.zh: 長慶襲世職，繼父領鄉團，先後從官軍克廬江、舒城，擢守備。

translations.literal: Changqing inherited the hereditary post, succeeded his father in leading local militia, and in succession followed the government army in taking Lujiang and Shucheng; he was promoted to garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing inherited the hereditary rank and took over his father's militia. He marched with imperial forces to capture Lujiang and Shucheng and was promoted to garrison commander.

sentences.zh: 十一年，會攻克三河。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he joined in capturing Sanhe.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he took part in the capture of Sanhe.

sentences.zh: 淮軍始創，領五百人，曰慶字營。

translations.literal: When the Huai Army was first created, he led five hundred men, called the Qingzi Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai Army was first formed, he commanded five hundred men in the Qingzi Battalion.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從李鴻章至上海，破賊於虹橋，克奉賢、南匯、川沙，又破寶山竄賊，超擢游擊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, defeated rebels at Hongqiao, took Fengxian, Nanhui, and Chuansha, again defeated rebels raiding from Baoshan, and was exceptionally promoted to acting major.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, routed rebels at Hongqiao, captured Fengxian, Nanhui, and Chuansha, beat back raiders from Baoshan, and was exceptionally promoted to brevet major.

sentences.zh: 二年，回籍募勇，會李秀成糾眾圍廬江，長慶登陴固守，出擊賊，走之。

translations.literal: In the second year he returned home to recruit braves; Li Xiucheng gathered troops to besiege Lujiang; Changqing mounted the walls to hold firm, sallied to strike rebels, and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he returned home to recruit troops. When Li Xiucheng besieged Lujiang, Changqing held the walls, sallied out, and drove the rebels away.

sentences.zh: 事定，率新募五營赴上海，進攻楓涇、西塘，克之，毀千窯賊巢，擢副將。

translations.literal: When affairs were settled he led five newly recruited battalions to Shanghai, advanced against Fengjing and Xitang, took them, destroyed the rebel nest at Qianyao, and was promoted to brigadier general.
translations.idiomatic: After order was restored he led five newly raised battalions to Shanghai, captured Fengjing and Xitang, destroyed the rebel stronghold at Qianyao, and was promoted to deputy commander.

sentences.zh: 規嘉善，破張涇匯賊壘。

translations.literal: Pressing Jiashan, he broke the rebel fort at Zhangjinghui.
translations.idiomatic: In operations against Jiashan he stormed the rebel stockade at Zhangjinghui.

sentences.zh: 三年，會攻嘉興，左臂中槍，督士卒緣城上，克之，以總兵記名，賜號力勇巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the third year he joined the attack on Jiaxing; his left arm took a shot; he directed soldiers up the wall along the city; it was taken; he was entered as major general and granted the title Liyong Batür.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined the assault on Jiaxing. Shot in the left arm, he still directed his men up the wall and took the city. He was nominated major general and granted the title Liyong Batür.

sentences.zh: 自是分兵援浙、閩，迭克郡縣。

translations.literal: From then on he divided forces to relieve Zhejiang and Fujian and in succession took prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he detached columns to support Zhejiang and Fujian and captured one prefecture and county after another.

sentences.zh: 五年，追敘以提督總兵侭先題奏。

translations.literal: In the fifth year retrospective deliberation placed him among provincial commanders and major generals to be memorialized first when vacancies arose.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his past service earned him a place among those to be first nominated when provincial commander or major general vacancies opened.

sentences.zh: 七年，從李鴻章剿捻匪，轉戰河南內黃、滑、濬，山東臨邑、德州，直隸寧津。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he followed Li Hongzhang in suppressing Nian bandits, fighting at Neihuang, Hua, and Jun in Henan, Linyi and Dezhou in Shandong, and Ningjin in Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he joined Li Hongzhang against the Nian, campaigning through Neihuang, Hua, and Jun in Henan, Linyi and Dezhou in Shandong, and Ningjin in Zhili.

sentences.zh: 捻平，賜黃馬褂，晉號瑚敦巴圖魯。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified, the yellow riding jacket was bestowed and he was advanced to the title Hudun Batür.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian were suppressed he was awarded the yellow riding jacket and promoted to the title Hudun Batür.

sentences.zh: 調防江北，駐軍徐州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to defend north of the Yangzi and garrisoned Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison the region north of the Yangzi, with headquarters at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，鼎軍譁變，長慶扼截，斬其倡亂者，眾懼服，分別資遣數千人，旬日而定。

translations.literal: In the eighth year the Ding Army mutinied; Changqing blocked and intercepted, beheaded the ringleaders, the masses feared and submitted, separately provided funds to dismiss several thousand men, and within ten days it was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year the Ding Army mutinied. Changqing intercepted them, executed the ringleaders, and within ten days had dismissed several thousand men with pay and restored order.

sentences.zh: 事聞，予議敘。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, deliberative reward was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, he was recommended for commendation.

sentences.zh: 九年，移駐揚州，丁母憂，予百日假，仍留軍濬鹽河，興水利。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he moved garrison to Yangzhou; in mourning for his mother he was granted a hundred days' leave yet still kept the army dredging the salt river and promoting water works.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he moved to Yangzhou. When his mother died he was granted a hundred days' mourning leave but remained with the army dredging the salt canal and promoting irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 尋复移屯江浦、江陰。

translations.literal: Before long he again moved camp to Jiangpu and Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon shifted his garrison to Jiangpu and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 十三年，增募四營築江陰、江寧砲台。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he recruited four more battalions to build batteries at Jiangyin and Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he raised four additional battalions to construct fortifications at Jiangyin and Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，授直隸正定鎮總兵，仍留防江南。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed commander of the Zhengding Garrison in Zhili yet still remained to defend Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was appointed commander of the Zhengding Garrison in Zhili while continuing to defend the Jiangnan region.

sentences.zh: 六合鄉民因漕重聚眾譁署，長慶馳至諭散，為請奏減漕額。

translations.literal: Villagers of Liuhe gathered in a crowd and stormed the yamen because grain transport levies were heavy; Changqing rushed there to instruct and disperse them and memorialized to reduce the transport quota.
translations.idiomatic: When villagers in Liuhe rioted over heavy grain transport levies, Changqing rushed to disperse them and memorialized for a reduction in the transport tax.

sentences.zh: 寧國教民白會清不法，激變，毀教堂，構訟。

translations.literal: In Ningguo the convert Bai Huiqing acted unlawfully, provoked an uprising, destroyed a church, and stirred litigation.
translations.idiomatic: In Ningguo the Christian convert Bai Huiqing broke the law, sparked a disturbance, destroyed a church, and set off a legal dispute.

sentences.zh: 建平人何渚被枉，長慶往按得實，為白於總督沈葆楨，平反之。

translations.literal: He Zhu of Jianping was wronged; Changqing went to investigate and found the truth, cleared the matter before Governor Shen Baozhen, and reversed the verdict.
translations.idiomatic: When He Zhu of Jianping was wrongfully convicted, Changqing investigated, established the facts, appealed to Governor Shen Baozhen, and secured his exoneration.

sentences.zh: 率士卒濬江浦黑水河、四泉河、玉帶河，兩年始畢工。

translations.literal: He led soldiers in dredging the Heishui, Siquan, and Yudai rivers at Jiangpu; the work took two years to finish.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops in dredging the Heishui, Siquan, and Yudai rivers at Jiangpu, a project that took two years to complete.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢浙江提督。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Zhejiang provincial commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to provincial military governor of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 尋調廣東水師提督，未之任，會法越軍事起，命幫辦山東軍務，四鎮皆歸節制，率所部屯登州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Guangdong naval commander-in-chief but did not take the post; when the Franco-Vietnamese war arose he was ordered to assist in Shandong military affairs; four garrisons all came under his command; he led his command to garrison Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to command the Guangdong naval forces but never took up that post. When the Franco-Vietnamese war broke out he was ordered to assist in Shandong military affairs with four garrisons under his command, and he encamped at Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 八年，朝鮮內亂，禁軍犯王宮，殺大臣，王妃失踪，燔日本使館，日本且發兵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year civil strife broke out in Korea; the palace guard stormed the royal palace, killed ministers, the queen consort disappeared, the Japanese legation was burned, and Japan was about to send troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year civil disorder erupted in Korea. Palace guards stormed the royal residence, killed ministers, the queen consort vanished, the Japanese legation was burned, and Japan prepared to send troops.

sentences.zh: 命長慶率兵艦三往按治，先日兵至。

translations.literal: Changqing was ordered to lead three warships to investigate and settle matters; Japanese troops arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was ordered to take three warships to restore order, but Japanese forces arrived first.

sentences.zh: 廉知事由朝鮮王父大院君李昰應所主，至則昰應尚踞王宮，來謁，留語及暮，遣隊擁赴海口，命兵艦致之天津，次日擊散亂黨，迎复王妃。

translations.literal: He had learned the affair was directed by the Korean royal father, the Grand Prince Heungseon Daewongun Yi Haung; on arrival Haung still held the palace and came to pay respects; Changqing detained him in conversation until evening, sent a detachment to escort him to the harbor, ordered a warship to deliver him to Tianjin; the next day he routed the disorderly faction and welcomed back the queen consort.
translations.idiomatic: Having learned that the trouble was instigated by the regent, Grand Prince Heungseon Daewongun Yi Haung, Changqing found Haung still in the palace when he arrived. He detained him in conversation until evening, then sent troops to escort him to the coast and a warship to carry him to Tianjin. The next day he dispersed the mutineers and restored the queen consort.

sentences.zh: 日本初欲藉故多所要挾，見事已定，氣為之沮。

translations.literal: Japan at first wished to use the pretext to make many demands; seeing the affair was settled, their spirit was dampened.
translations.idiomatic: Japan had initially hoped to exploit the crisis for extensive concessions, but when the situation was resolved their leverage collapsed.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉其功，予三等輕車都尉世職，遂留鎮漢城。

translations.literal: An edict praised his merit, granted the hereditary post of third-rank Commandant of Light Chariots, and he then remained to garrison Hanseong.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended his achievement, granted the hereditary rank of third-rank Commandant of Light Chariots, and he remained to garrison Seoul.

sentences.zh: 長慶在朝鮮兩年，修治道塗，救災恤民，示以恩信，國人感之。

translations.literal: Changqing was in Korea two years, repaired roads, relieved disasters and comforted the people, showed favor and trust, and the people of the country were moved.
translations.idiomatic: During two years in Korea, Changqing repaired roads, relieved disasters, cared for the populace, and won their trust through consistent goodwill.

sentences.zh: 十年，命移防金州，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was ordered to transfer defense to Jinzhou; before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was ordered to garrison Jinzhou; he died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 詔優恤，建專祠，諡武壯，予其次子保初主事。

translations.literal: An edict granted favorable mourning favors, built a dedicated shrine, posthumous title Wuzhuang, and gave his second son Baochu the post of secretary in the main office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted generous posthumous honors, a dedicated shrine was erected, he received the posthumous name Wuzhuang (Martial and Stalwart), and his second son Baochu was given a secretariat post at court.

sentences.zh: 保初後官刑部，上書言時政，辭職歸。

translations.literal: Baochu later served in the Ministry of Justice, memorialized on current affairs, resigned his post, and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Baochu later served in the Ministry of Justice, submitted a memorial on current affairs, resigned, and returned home.

sentences.zh: 長慶好讀書，愛士，時稱儒將。

translations.literal: Changqing loved reading books and cherished scholars; of the time he was called a Confucian general.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was a devoted reader who valued cultivated men and was known as a scholar-general.

sentences.zh: 保初亦文雅，有文風。

translations.literal: Baochu was also refined and elegant and had literary style.
translations.idiomatic: Baochu was likewise refined and showed a genuine literary sensibility.

sentences.zh: 論曰：李鴻章創立淮軍，一時人材蔚起，程學啟實為之魁，功成身殞，開軍遂微。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Li Hongzhang founded the Huai Army; for a time talent flourished together; Cheng Xueqi was truly its foremost leader; merit accomplished, body perished, and the Kai Battalion army thereafter declined.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: When Li Hongzhang founded the Huai Army, talent rose in abundance, and Cheng Xueqi stood at its head. He died just as his greatest triumph was won, and the Kai Battalion force he had built never recovered its former strength.

sentences.zh: 銘軍最稱勁旅，樹軍、盛軍、鼎軍亦各驂靳。

translations.literal: The Ming Army was most called a crack force; the Shu, Sheng, and Ding armies each also ran abreast.
translations.idiomatic: The Ming Battalion was regarded as the hardest-fighting unit, while the Shu, Sheng, and Ding forces each kept pace close behind.

sentences.zh: 粵寇平而捻匪熾，曾國籓欲全湘軍末路，主專用淮軍，平捻多賴其力。

translations.literal: When Cantonese rebels were pacified the Nian bandits flared; Zeng Guofan wished to preserve the Xiang Army's final path, advocated relying chiefly on the Huai Army, and pacifying the Nian depended much on its strength.
translations.idiomatic: After the Taiping rebels were suppressed the Nian rebellion intensified. Zeng Guofan sought to preserve the Xiang Army's legacy but argued for relying chiefly on the Huai Army, whose strength proved decisive in suppressing the Nian.

sentences.zh: 其後北洋籌防，全倚淮軍，而以盛軍為之中堅。

translations.literal: Afterward in Beiyang coastal defense planning, all relied on the Huai Army, with the Sheng Army as its central pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Beiyang coastal defenses were organized, the Huai Army bore the entire burden, with the Sheng Battalion as its core.

sentences.zh: 劉銘傳才氣無雙，不居人下，故易退難進。

translations.literal: Liu Mingchuan's talent and spirit were without peer; he would not place himself below others; therefore he easily withdrew and was hard to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mingchuan's talent was unmatched and he would bow to no one, which made him quick to withdraw from office and slow to accept promotion.

sentences.zh: 守台治台，自有建樹。

translations.literal: In defending and governing Taiwan he had achievements of his own.
translations.idiomatic: In defending and governing Taiwan he left achievements of his own.

sentences.zh: 二張、二周，治軍皆有家法。

translations.literal: The two Zhangs and two Zhous each had household methods in governing troops.
translations.idiomatic: The two Zhang brothers and two Zhou brothers each commanded troops by methods all their own.

sentences.zh: 潘鼎新防邊失律，不保令名。

translations.literal: Pan Dingxin in border defense breached discipline and did not preserve a fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Dingxin discredited himself through disciplinary failures on the frontier and did not preserve his good name.

sentences.zh: 吳長慶戰績雖亞諸人，朝鮮定亂，能弭大變。

translations.literal: Wu Changqing's battle record, though second to the others, in settling disorder in Korea was able to quell a great upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Changqing's battlefield record ranked below the others, but in quelling the Korean crisis he averted a far greater catastrophe.

sentences.zh: 及甲午邊釁起，宿將彫零，衛汝貴、葉志超等庸才僨事，為全軍之玷。

translations.literal: When the Jiawu border crisis arose, veteran generals were scattered and few; Wei Rugui, Ye Zhichao, and other mediocre talents ruined affairs and were a stain on the whole army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sino-Japanese War of 1894 broke out, the old generals were gone. Mediocrities such as Wei Rugui and Ye Zhichao bungled the campaign and brought disgrace on the entire force.

sentences.zh: 後起僅一聶士成，庚子殉難，淮軍遂熸。

translations.literal: Among later risers there was only Nie Shicheng; he died for the realm in Gengzi and the Huai Army was then extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Among the later generation only Nie Shicheng distinguished himself; he died in the Boxer crisis of 1900, and the Huai Army passed into extinction.

sentences.zh: 四十年中，盛衰得失，於此見焉。

translations.literal: Within forty years, rise and fall, gain and loss, are seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: Within the space of forty years, its rise and fall, its gains and losses, may all be read here.
